sections.title: 翻译
sections.passage:
1 They were, by far, the largest and most distant objects that scientists had ever detected: a strip of enormous cosmic clouds some 15 billion light-years from earth. 2 But even more important, it was the farthest that scientists had been able to look into the past, for what they were seeing were the patterns and structures that existed 15 billion years ago.? 3 That was just about the moment that the universe was born. 4 What the researchers found was at once both amazing and expected: the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s Cosmic Background Explorer satellite — Cobe — had discovered landmark evidence that the universe did in fact begin with the primeval explosion that has become known as the Big Bang (the theory that the universe originated in an explosion from a single mass of energy).
1 The existence of the giant clouds was virtually required for the Big Bang, first put forward in the 1920s, to maintain its reign as the dominant explanation of the cosmos.? 2 According to the theory, the universe burst into being as a submicroscopic, unimaginably dense knot of pure energy that flew outward in all directions, emitting radiation as it went, condensing into particles and then into atoms of gas. 3 Over billions of years, the gas was compressed by gravity into galaxies, stars, plants and eventually, even humans.
1 Cobe is designed to see just the biggest structures, but astronomers would like to see much smaller hot spots as well, the seeds of local objects like clusters and superclusters of galaxies. 2 They shouldn’t have long to wait. 3 Astrophysicists working with ground-based detectors at the South Pole and balloon-borne instruments are closing in on such structures, and may report their findings soon.?
1 If the small hot spots look as expected, that will be a triumph for yet another scientific idea, a refinement of the Big Bang called the inflationary universe theory.? 2 Inflation says that very early on, the universe expanded in size by more than a trillion trillion trillion trillionfold in much less than a second, propelled by a sort of antigravity. 3 Odd though it sounds, cosmic inflation is a scientifically plausible consequence of some respected ideas in elementary particle physics, and many astrophysicists have been convinced for the better part of a decade that it is true.?

questions.stem:
① “到目前为止，它们是科学家所探测到的最大且最遥远的天体：一片巨大的宇宙云，距离地球约 150 亿光年。”②但更为重要的是，这是科学家们所能观测到的最遥远的过去，因为他们看到的是150亿年前就存在的星系的形状和结构。③ 那差不多就是宇宙诞生的时刻。④ 研究人员的发现既令人惊叹又在意料之中：美国国家航空航天局的宇宙背景探索者卫星（COBE）发现了具有里程碑意义的证据，证明宇宙确实起源于最初的一次爆炸，即人们所知的“大爆炸”（该理论认为宇宙源于一团单一能量的爆炸）。
① 实际上，巨大的宇宙云的存在，是20世纪20年代首创的“大爆炸论”得以保持其宇宙起源论的主导地位所不可或缺的。② 根据该理论，宇宙源于一个亚微观的、密度大到难以想象的纯能量团，它在向四面八方发散的过程中发射出辐射线，逐渐凝聚成粒子，进而形成气体原子。③ 数十亿年来，这种气体在引力的作用下被压缩，形成了星系、恒星、行星，最终甚至形成了人类。
① COBE 卫星的设计目标仅为观测最大尺度的宇宙结构，但天文学家还希望能观测到小得多的热点区域 —— 这些区域正是星系团、超星系团等局部天体的形成 “种子”。② 他们可能不必长期等待。③ 天体物理学家们使用南极陆基探测器及球载仪器进行观测，正越来越接近这些云系，也许不久他们就会报告其观测结果。
① 若这些小热点区域与预期一致，那将是另一科学理论的胜利 —— 该理论���‘大爆炸理论’的修正版，即‘宇宙暴胀理论‘。② “宇宙暴胀理论” 认为，在宇宙诞生初期，一种类似反引力的力量推动着宇宙，使其在不到一秒的时间内，尺寸膨胀了超过1万亿亿亿亿倍。③ 尽管听起来有些奇怪，但宇宙膨胀是基本粒子物理学中一些公认观点在科学上合理的推论，而且十多年来，许多天体物理学家一直坚信这一观点是正确的。
questions.answer: 但是更为重要的是，这是科学家们所能观测到的最遥远的过去景象，因为他们看到的是150亿年前宇宙云系的形状和结构。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“But even more important,”在整个句子中做状语，But意为但是，然而， even more important,为比较级结构，译为但更为重要。“it was the farthest that scientists had been able to look into the past”中it具有指代意义，指上句提到的离地球约150亿光年的巨大宇宙云系，可译为这，look into the past意为观察过去的，即处理为“这是科学家们所能观测到的最遥远的景象。”，“for what they were seeing were the patterns and structures that existed 15 billion years ago. ”这是由for连接的第二个并列分句，for译为因为，表原因，其次，此部分是主系表结构，可按照“...是...”结构译出。最后，patterns and structures意为形状和结构。即译为因为他们看到的是宇宙云系的形状和结构。

【句子结构分析】

“The existence of the giant clouds was virtually required for the Big Bang”中The existence of the giant clouds 为主语，译为巨大的宇宙云的存在，virtually为副词，意为事实上，实际上，作状语，故可置于句首或句中。此外，was...required为一般过去式的被动语态，为了符合汉语表达习惯可以意译为是...所不可或缺的。“ first put forward in the 1920s”此部分为过去分词短语作定语，修饰the Big Bang，即译为20世纪20年代首创的。“to maintain its reign as the dominant explanation of the cosmos. ”中to maintain its reign as 意为以保持...的主导地位， explanation of the cosmos. 可直译为对于宇宙的解释。

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“Astrophysicists working with ground-based detectors at the South Pole and balloon-borne instruments”中working with...and ...instruments是现在分词短语作后置定语，修饰主语Astrophysicists ，在实际上是表示其所用的研究工具，所以可译为用/使用...， at the South Pole 可以直译为在南极，但由于其修饰ground-based instruments可以译为球载仪器，故这部分可译为“天体物理学家们使用南极陆基探测器及球载仪器进行观测。“are closing in on such structures,”中close in（on)意为come nearer and attack from several directions,这里是一个比喻用法，可以意译为越来越接近，structures要结合上下文，译为云系，团状物质。“and may report their findings soon.”their指代前一个分句的主语Astrophysicists ，译为他们，findings即为观测结果，这部分译为也许不久他们就会报告其观测结果。

questions.answer: 假如那些小热点看上去同预计的一样，那将是又一个科学论说的重大成就，即更完美的大爆炸论，亦称“宇宙膨胀说”。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“If the small hot spots look as expected, ”为if引导的条件状语从句，as expected 是一种习惯用法，意为正如预料的那样，“that will be a triumph for yet another scientific idea”这部分是主系表结构，可译为那将是又一科学论说的重大成就。“a refinement of the Big Bang called the inflationary universe theory. ”这部分是scientific idea的同位语，可使用即、也就是，等词将其译出，called...theory为过去分词，作a refinement of the Big Bang的后置定语，可以译为前置定语，故这部分可译为即更完美的大爆炸论，亦称“宇宙膨胀说”。

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“ Odd though it sounds”中it指代cosmic inflation，though表让步，故译为“宇宙膨胀说‘虽然听似奇特”。“cosmic inflation is a scientifically plausible consequence of some respected ideas in elementary particle physics”中cosmic inflation译为宇宙膨胀说，consequence的本意为结果、后果，此处可引申为推论，plausible consequence即为可信度推论，respected idea的本意是受人尊敬的想法或思想，引申为公认的理论。即这部分可调整为但它是基本粒子物理学中一些公认的理论在科学上看来可信的推论。“and many astrophysicists have been convinced for the better part of a decade that it is true.”中it仍然指代cosmic inflation，译为这一论说，for the better part of a decade 译为近十年来，故这部分译为许多天体物理学家近十年来一直确信这一论说是正确的。

sections.title: 完型填空
sections.passage:
1 Until recently most historians spoke very critically of the Industrial Revolution.   2 They 1 that in the long run industrialization greatly raised the standard of living for the 2 man.? 3 But they insisted that its 3 results during the period from 1750 to 1850 were widespread poverty and misery for the 4 of the English population.? 4 5 contrast, they saw in the preceding hundred years from 1650 to 1750, when England was still a 6 agricultural country, a period of great abundance and prosperity.?
1 This view, 7, is generally thought to be wrong.? 2 Specialists 8 history and economics, have 9 two things: that the period from 1650 to 1750 was 10 by great poverty, and that industrialization certainly did not worsen and may have actually improved the conditions for the majority of the populace.?

questions.explanation:
【答案解析】

空格前一句提到：大多数历史学家都猛烈抨击工业革命。空格所在句意为：从长远来看，工业化极大地提高了群众的生活水平，显然这不是对工业革命的抨击；紧接着空格后一句以“But”表转折，点明抨击内容。由此可知，空格所在句和后一句是对空格前一句的具体说明，而空格所在句与后一句之间为让步转折关系。浏览备选项，能满足此逻辑关系的只有A选项admitted（承认），故A选项正确。B选项believed（相信）和C选项claimed（宣称）后面跟的内容都是肯定的观点，由文中的spoke very critically（猛烈抨击）可知历史学家对工业革命持否定态度，故均予以排除。D选项predicted（预言，预测）表示对未发生的事情进行推测、预测，不符合上下文语义逻辑，故排除。

【答案解析】

空格处所在句说明，从长远来看，工业化极大地提高了____群众的生活水平。根据常识，工业革命影响的对象是普通老百姓，因此可知，空格处表达的是“普通人”之意。四个备选项中只有B选项average修饰人时指“普通老百姓”，符合语义，故B选项正确。A选项plain意为“平的；简单的”，一般不用来修饰人，如用来修饰人，意为“不漂亮的”；C选项mean修饰人时，意为“命鄙的；吝啬的”，这两个选项都与原文语义不符，故均排除。D选项normal意为“正常的；标准的”，侧重于描述身心的正常，故排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句中的were一词表明其前后内容相对应，即its____results=widespread poverty and misery。��据常识，“普遍的贫穷和苦难”应是industrialization“直接”引起的结果。浏览备选项，能表达“直接”之意的只有D选项immediate，故D选项正确。A选项momentary（短暂的），B选项prompt（迅速的）和C选项instant（立即的）均表示短暂时间，而文中的during the period from 1750 to 1850（一百年）表明结果持续时间并不短，显然矛盾，均予以排除

【答案解析】

历史学家对工业化持批判态度，故其可能坚持认为“工业化给大多数英国人带来了贫穷和苦难”。因而，从结构上看，空格所填词要与the和of构成短语“the...of”，并且要修饰不可数名词population；从语义上看，“the...of”的意思应为“大多数，大部分”。A选项bulk意为“大部分”，the bulk of是固定搭配，意为大多数，相当于the majority of，恰与其前的widespread语义上相呼应，故A选项正确。B选项host可构成短语a host of/hosts of，意为“许多”，多用于修饰可数名词，且不能被the修饰；C选项gross表示“总共的”时，通常用于金钱方面，且不能与the和of搭配；D选项magnitude意为“大小”，the magnitude of强调某物的尺寸、规模，故都排除。

【答案解析】

空格前一句指出1750至1850年，工业革命带来的是贫穷和苦难；而空格所在句提到1650至1750年英国的富裕和繁荣（great abundance and prosperity），前后两部分形成鲜明对比。而D选项By与contrast搭配，组成的短语By contrast（对比起来，与之相比）符合文意，故正确。A选项On、B选项With和C选项For都不能与contrast搭配，故都排除。

【答案解析】

分析空格所在句，其指出英国在1650至1750年是一个农业国，空格处需填入一个副词来修饰形容词agricultural。那么，空格处所填的副词应是表示农业国的程度或范围。D选项completely意为“完全地”，强调程度，故正确。A选项broadly（一般而言；大体上）一般用来表示某一道理、观点或意见等“大体如此”，不能表程度；B选项thoroughly（彻底地）强调“不留一点余地”，用在此处修饰agricultural过于绝对；C选项generally（通常；多数时候）一般不修饰形容词，且与agricultural不能构成符合逻辑的语义搭配，故三个选项都排除。

【答案解析】

浏览备选项，空格处需填入一个逻辑关系词，那么，本题解答的关键在于分析空格所在句与上文的关系。从上下文来看，空格所在句中的This view即为上段历史学家的观点（即抨击工业革命），而空格所在句直接反驳这种观点，说其是错误的。可见，上下文应为转折关系，空格处需填入一个表转折的副词，故A选项however（然而）正确。B选项meanwhile（同时）表时间关系；C选项therefore（因此）表因果关系；D选项moreover（而且）表递进关系，都不符合文章的逻辑要求，均予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格前为Specialists（专家），空格后为学科（history and economics），因此要填一个介词��Specialists和history and economics衔接起来。B选项in与Specialists连用，可表示“在某方面的专家”，故B选项正确。A选项at与specialists连用，常表示“某个地方的专家”；C选项about用作介词的意思是“关于；在……附近”；D选项for则常表示“目的”或“对……而言”，都不符合语境，均予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格前一句表明：人们普遍认为这种观点是错误的；空格所在句中，其主语是Specialists，宾语是two things（两件事），且冒号后具体阐述了two things。可见，空格所在句论述的内容是为了证明前一句的观点。而two things均属于事实，那么，专家应该是“摆出”事实，以证明上句观点，故C选项shown（展示，摆出）符合语境，为正确答案。A选项manifested（展现，展示）一般指的是显示出某种情感或态度，而文中则是提出观点；B选项approved意为“赞同，同意”，专家不可能同意“极度贫困”这一事实；D选项speculated意为“推测，想到”，为不及物动词，一般与on或about搭配，故都排除。

【答案解析】

浏览备选项并结合空格所在句可知，本空需填入一个动词的过去分词将the period和by great poverty衔接起来。由上下文语义可知，great poverty是the period的一个特征。D选项marked代入文中，表示“该时期的特征是极度贫穷”，故正确。A选项noted，意为“注意”，一般与for或as搭配；B选项impressed意为“给……以深刻印象”，常与on，upon或with搭配；两者均不与by搭配，故都排除。C选项labeled意为“贴上标签”，与by搭配构成词组labeled by...，意为“由……贴上标签”，不符合语义，故排除。

sections.title: 写作 Part B
sections.passage:
1 A hen in the picture is holding a notice promising that her eggs would be round and surely would contain egg shells, egg whites and yolks. 【描述图画1：整体描述】 2 Those promised qualities are only basic components of eggs. 【描述图画2：细节描述】 3 How ridiculous it is! 【图画评价：荒谬】
1 Under the funny appearance hides a serious social problem that there are many meaningless promises which only reflect the basic responsibilities of the promise makers. 【2段主旨-指出图画反应的社会现象】 2 Manufacturing units guarantee to turn out products of good quality; commercial enterprises swear to provide genuine commodities and enthusiastic services; administration departments assure to perform their tasks effectively and fairly without taking any bribery. 【举例论证-生厂商/工商企业/政府部门】
1 Such promises are deceptive to the public. 【引入作者观点：这些承诺对社会有害】 2 The hen and likes should know that by dishonest words no one could survive the intense competition under market economy system. 【递进：不诚实的言语是无法生存】 3 On one hand, people engaged in providing all kinds of services should honestly inform their customers of the services that they can enjoy because mutual trust is the foundation of business. 【建议1：商业服务应诚实对待客户】 4 They should remember the old saying," Honesty is the best policy." 【引用论证：诚实的重要性】 5 On the other hand, necessary laws and regulations should be adopted and enforced to ensure a trust-worthy economic and social environment. 【建议2：法律+规章制度】 6 Only in these ways, can both parties, service providers and those served, enjoy a healthy atmosphere of mutual trust. 【展望未来】

sections.title: 阅读Text1
sections.passage:
1 Few creations of big technology capture the imagination like giant dams. 2 Perhaps it is humankind ’s long suffering at the mercy of flood and drought that makes the ideal of forcing the waters to do our bidding so fascinating. 3 But to be fascinated is also, sometimes, to be blind. 4 Several giant dam projects threaten to do more harm than good.?
1 The lesson from dams is that big is not always beautiful. 2 It doesn’t help that building a big, powerful dam has become a symbol of achievement for nations and people striving to assert themselves. 3 Egypt ’s leadership in the Arab world was cemented by the Aswan High Dam. 4 Turkey ’s bid for First World status includes the giant Ataturk Dam.
1 But big dams tend not to work as intended. 2 The Aswan Dam, for example, stopped the Nile flooding but deprived Egypt of the fertile silt that floods left — all in return for a giant reservoir of disease which is now so full of silt that it barely generates electricity.
1 And yet, the myth of controlling the waters persists. 2 This week, in the heart of civilized Europe, Slovaks and Hungarians stopped just short of sending in the troops in their contention over a dam on the Danube. 3 The huge complex will probably have all the usual problems of big dams. 4 But Slovakia is bidding for independence from the Czechs, and now needs a dam to prove itself.
1 Meanwhile, in India, the World Bank has given the go-ahead to the even more wrong-headed Narmada Dam. 2 And the bank has done this even though its advisors say the dam will cause hardship for the powerless and environmental destruction.? 3 The benefits are for the powerful, but they are far from guaranteed.
1 Proper, scientific study of the impacts of dams and of the costs and benefits of controlling water can help to resolve these conflicts. 2 Hydroelectric power and flood control and irrigation are possible without building monster dams. 3 But when you are dealing with myths, it is hard to be either proper, or scientific.? 4 It is time that the world learned the lessons of Aswan. 5 You don’t need a dam to be saved.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: people would be happy if they shut their eyes to reality

choices.label: B
choices.text: the blind could be happier than the sighted

choices.label: C
choices.text: over-excited people tend to neglect vital things

choices.label: D
choices.text: fascination makes people lose their eyesight

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. people would be happy if they shut their eyes to reality

    如果人们不理会现实，他们将会很高兴

B. the blind could be happier than the sighted

    盲人可能比看得见的人更高兴

C. over一excited people tend to neglect vital things

    过分激动的人易于忽视至关重要的事

D. fascination makes people lose their eyesight

    着迷使人们丧失视力


【定位及答案】

由题干定位至1段3句。此题需结合上下文进行分析。1段2句提到“驾驭洪水的这种理想如此让人着迷”，这与3句中的to be fascinated相对应，可见此处是说修建水坝让人着迷;紧接着1段4句“一些巨型水坝工程存在弊大于利的潜在危险”解释了3句中的is also…to be blind,可见水坝的弊端容易被忽视。由此推断，3句言下之意是:人在过分激动时往往会忽视至关重要的东西。故C选项是对上述内容的合理推断，为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【因果倒置】A如果人们不理会现实，他们将会很高兴： 由1段2句和4句可知，2句旨在说明过分激动时会变得盲目，故排除。

【答非所问&望文生义】B、D两个选项是根据1段3句中blind(盲目的)一词的字面意思所做的关于“盲人”、“视力”的无关联想，均与题干无关，故均排除。

choices.label: D
choices.text: common people in the Narmada Dam area

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. areas short of electricity

    缺电的地区

B. dams without power stations

    无发电站的水坝

C. poor countries around India

    印度周边贫困的国家

D. common people in the Narmada Dam area

    纳尔马达大坝地区的平民百姓


【定位及答案】

题干已定位到5段。从语法角度看定冠词the加形容词多用于指代具有某种属性的一类人，那么the powerless指代具有“无能为力”特点的一类人：从语义角度看，5段2句的Cause hard ship for the powerless和3句的The benefits are for the powerless表意相反；后者指“利益归有权有势者所有”，前者应指“给无权无势的人造成苦难”，再结合5段1句的背景“世界银行已同意贷款给印度来修建问题更多的纳尔马达大坝”可推断，“无权无势的人”指的应是纳尔马达大坝地区的平民百姓，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【词汇干扰】A选项和B选项均是根据5段2句中的power（电）和less（没有；缺失）捏造出来的意思，均与原词义“无权无势的无关”，故排除。

【无中生有】C 印度周边贫困的国家：原文未提“印度周边贫困的国家”，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: They bring in more fertile soil.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They have universal control of the waters.

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. They bring in more fertile soil.

    它们带来更多的肥沃土壤

B. They help defend the country.

    它们帮助保卫国家

C. They strengthen international ties.

    它们加强了国际关系

D. They have universal control of the waters.

    它们全面控制了洪水


【定位及答案】

由the myth可定位至4段1句，该句指出“控制水的错误观点还在继续”，说明错误观点与“控制水”相关；紧接着4段和5段分别利用多瑙河大坝和纳尔马达大坝的例子来说明这种错误观点仍在继续，这表明错误的观点是利用大型水坝控制洪水。此外，6段3句再次提及myth，指出人们面对只要有大坝就能控制洪水这种错误观点时缺乏理智。由此也可说明，错误观点即利用大坝控制洪水，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 它们带来更多的肥沃土壤：3段2句提到尽管The Aswan Dam阻止了尼罗河洪水的泛滥，但也使埃及失去了肥沃淤泥，故排除。

【答非所问】B 它们帮助保卫国家：4段2句提及“动用军队”是因为两国就多瑙河水坝的修建问题产生争执，这与保卫国家无关，故排除B选项。

【答非所问】C 它们加强了国际关系：2段3、4句指出埃及因阿斯旺大坝而巩固了其领导地位，土耳其为跻身第一世界而修建阿塔图尔克大坝，这说明修建大坝已成为国家竭力显示自己权威的标志（1段3句），而不是“加强国际关系”，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: “It's no use crying over spilt milk”

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A.“It's no use crying over spilt milk”

    “覆水难收”

B.“More haste, less speed”

    “欲速则不达”生有

C. “Look before you leap”

    “三思而后行”

D.“He who laughs last laughs best”

    “谁笑到最后，谁笑得最好”


【定位及答案】

1段引出话题指出人们对建造水坝盲目着迷，但建坝弊大于利；2、3段指出盲目建坝的恶果及教训；4、5段以多瑙河大坝和纳尔马达大坝为例指出人们对大坝的迷恋仍在继续；6段呼吁人们吸取历史教训，切勿盲目建坝。综上，文章强调建造大坝的弊端，旨在奉劝想建造大坝的各国政府要“三思而后行”，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A “覆水难收” ：作者在文中通过指出大坝的诸多弊端呼吁人们吸取教训，切勿盲目建坝以免继续犯错，这是作者的意图，而并非强调“覆水难收”，故A选项错误。

【无中生有】“欲速则不达”（即越想快速建成水坝就越无法建成）和“谁笑到最后，谁笑得最好”（即坚持到最后才能建成大坝）均与作者“呼吁切勿盲目建坝”这写作意图不符故排除B、D。

sections.title: 阅读Text2
sections.passage:
1 Well, no gain without pain, they say. 2 But what about pain without gain? 3 Everywhere you go in America, you hear tales of corporate revival. 4 What is harder to establish is whether the productivity revolution that businessmen assume they are presiding over is for real.?
1 The official statistics are mildly discouraging. 2 They show that, if you lump manufacturing and services together, productivity has grown on average by 1.2% since 1987. 3 That is somewhat faster than the average during the previous decade. 4 And since 1991, productivity has increased by about 2% a year, which is more than twice the 1978—1987 average. 5 The trouble is that part of the recent acceleration is due to the usual rebound that occurs at this point in a business cycle, and so is not conclusive evidence of a revival in the underlying trend.? 6 There is, as Robert Rubin, the treasury secretary, says, a “ disjunction ” between the mass of business anecdote that points to a leap in productivity and the picture reflected by the statistics.?
1 Some of this can be easily explained. 2 New ways of organizing the workplace — all that re-engineering and downsizing — are only one contribution to the overall productivity of an economy, which is driven by many other factors such as joint investment in equipment and machinery, new technology, and investment in education and training. 3 Moreover, most of the changes that companies make are intended to keep them profitable, and this need not always mean increasing productivity: switching to new markets or improving quality can matter just as much.
1 Two other explanations are more speculative. 2 First, some of the business restructuring of recent years may have been ineptly done. 3 Second, even if it was well done, it may have spread much less widely than people suppose.
1 Leonard Schlesinger, a Harvard academic and former chief executive of Au Bong Pain, a rapidly growing chain of bakery cafes, says that much “ re-engineering ” has been crude. 2 In many cases, he believes, the loss of revenue has been greater than the reductions in cost. 3 His colleague, Michael Beer, says that far too many companies have applied re-engineering in a mechanistic fashion, chopping out costs without giving sufficient thought to long-term profitability. 4 BBDO ’s Al Rosenshine is blunter. 5 He dismisses a lot of the work of re-engineering consultants as mere rubbish — “ the worst sort of ambulance chasing.”?

choices.label: A
choices.text: not as good as it seems

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. not as good as it seems

    不像它表面看起来那么好

B. at its turning point

    正处于转折点

C. much better than it seems

    比看起来要好得多

D. near to complete recovery

    几乎要实现全面复苏了


【定位及答案】

由题干可定位至2段。2段1句指出，官方的统计数字有些令人沮丧。接着2至4句通过官方数据表明美国的生产率指数不断上升；5句则指出，但这并不是真正的上升，而是经济的周期性反弹所造成的假象。由此概括，美国的经济状况并不像它表面上所显示的那样好，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】B 正处于转折点：选项原文未提及，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 比看起来要好得多：2段5句指出美国的经济并非想象中的那么好，而C选项表意与之相悖，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 几乎要实现全面复苏了：由2段5句“它不足以证明经济复。可知，美国根本没有出现经济复苏，更谈不上全面复苏，故D排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: exclude the usual rebound in a business cycle

choices.label: C
choices.text: meet the expectation of business people

choices.label: D
choices.text: fail to reflect the true state of economy

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. exclude the usual rebound in a business cycle

    排除了商业循环中常见的反弹

B. fall short of businessmen's anticipation

    没有达到商人们的期望

C. meet the expectation of business people

    达到了商人们的期望

D. fail to reflect the true state of economy

    没有反映出经济的真实状况


【定位及答案】

由offcial statistics可定位至第2，2段6句指出，有关生产率大幅度提高的商业传奇与统计数字所反映的情况之间存在着“脱节”。换言之，在生产率增长的问题上，政府统计的资料与口口相传的商业传奇不相待，即数据所反映的生产率增长并未达到商人们的期望。B选项是对此的间义转述，故正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 排除了商业循环中常见的反弹：1段6句表明、生产本增长的部分原因归结于经济发展的周期性反弹，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 达到了商人们的期望：2段6句指出，有关生产率大幅度提高的商业传奇与统计数字所反映的情况之间存在着“脱节”。换言之，政府的统计数字来达到商人们的期望，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 没有反映出经济的真实状况：2段6句指出，生严率大概度提体的商业传奇与数据不相符，而D选项说真实的经济状况与数据不符，属于偷换概念，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. he questions the truth of “no gain without pain"

    他质疑“不劳无获”的真实性

B. he does not think the productivity revolution works

    他认为生产力革命并未取得预期效果

C. he wonders if the official statistics are misleading

   他怀疑官方统计数据有误导性

D. he has conclusive evidence for the revival of businesses

    他有表明经济复苏的确凿证据


【定位及答案】

由what about pain with out gain可定位至1段2句。1段3、4句分别解释了2句的pain和gain，故pain指代生产力革命，gain指代企业复苏。而3、4、5段主要讨论了重组等生产力革命并未使企业取得预期效果（即实现经济复苏）的原因。由此概括，作者提出“劳而无获”意为“生产力革命并未取得预期效果”，故B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【断章取义】A 他质疑“不劳无获”的真实性：选项把1段1、2两句的字面意思（不劳无获、劳而无获）当成了作者的真正用意，故排除。

【过度推理】C 他怀疑官方统计数据有误导性：2段5句指出，反映经济增长的官方数据不是经济复苏的确凿证据，这表明官方数据无法证明经济复苏，而不能由此推出其具有误导性，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 他有表明经济复苏的确凿证据：选项与2段5句的so is not conclusive evidence表意相悖，故排除。

本题要求选出文中未提到内容，这类题目可使用排除法。3、4、5段只说明促进生产力革命的措施并未奏效，但并未提及激进的改革这一一问题，故A选项文中未提到，为正确答案。

sections.passage:
1 Science has long had an uneasy relationship with other aspects of culture. 2 Think of Gallileo’s 17th-century trial for his rebelling belief before the Catholic Church or poet William Blake’s harsh remarks against the mechanistic worldview of Isaac Newton. 3 The schism between science and the humanities has, if anything, deepened in this century.?
1 Until recently, the scientific community was so powerful that it could afford to ignore its critics — but no longer. 2 As funding for science has declined, scientists have attacked “anti-science” in several books, notably Higher Superstition, by Paul R. Gross, a biologist at the University of Virginia, and Norman Levitt, a mathematician at Rutgers University; and The Demon-Haunted World, by Carl Sagan of Cornell University.
1 Defenders of science have also voiced their concerns at meetings such as “ The Flight from Science and Reason,” held in New York City in 1995, and “ Science in the Age of (Mis) information,” which assembled last June near Buffalo.?
1 Anti-science clearly means different things to different people. 2 Gross and Levitt find fault primarily with sociologists, philosophers and other academics who have questioned science ’s objectivity. 3 Sagan is more concerned with those who believe in ghosts, creationism and other phenomena that contradict the scientific worldview.
1 A survey of news stories in 1996 reveals that the anti-science tag has been attached to many other groups as well, from authorities who advocated the elimination of the last remaining stocks of smallpox virus to Republicans who advocated decreased funding for basic research.
1 Few would dispute that the term applies to the Unabomber, whose manifesto, published in 1995, scorns science and longs for return to a pre-technological utopia. 2 But surely that does not mean environmentalists concerned about uncontrolled industrial growth are anti-science, as an essay in US News & World Report last May seemed to suggest.?
1 The environmentalists, inevitably, respond to such critics. 2 The true enemies of science, argues Paul Ehrlich of Stanford University, a pioneer of environmental studies, are those who question the evidence supporting global warming, the depletion of the ozone layer and other consequences of industrial growth.
1 Indeed, some observers fear that the anti-science epithet is in danger of becoming meaningless. 2 “The term ‘ anti-science ’ can lump together too many, quite different things,” notes Harvard University philosopher Gerald Holton in his 1993 work Science and Anti-Science. “ 3 They have in common only one thing that they tend to annoy or threaten those who regard themselves as more enlightened.”?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. confrontation    对抗

B. Dissatisfaction    不满

C. Separation    分歧

D. Contempt     轻视


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息定位至1段。1段的三句话为总分总结构：1句提到科学与文化的其他方面之间的关系一向很紧张，2句举例证明此观点，3句提到本世纪自然科学与人文学科之间的schism更深了。可见，1、3句在内容（Long和in this century , other aspects of culture 和humanities,uneasy relationship和schism）上相呼应，根据常识，两方关系紧张是因为其间存在矛盾，即两派因意见上有分歧而产生矛盾，故“schism”指自然科学与人文学科之间的分歧，故C选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 对抗：只有分歧才能“加深”，而对抗只能“加强”，因此不能说confrontation deepened，故排除。

【答非所问】B、D两个选项均代表1段3句所举例子中人物的态度，且不能由一。段1、3句的“自然科学和人文学科之间存在矛盾”而推出两派之间存在不满或彼此轻视，故均排除。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. discuss the cause of the decline of science's power

    讨论科学影响力下降的原因

B. show the author's sympathy with scientists

    表示作者对科学家的同情

C. explain the way in which science develops

    说明科学发展的方式

D. exemplify the division of science and the humanities

    举例说明自然科学和人文学科的分歧


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息可定位至2、3段。2段指出科学家们著书抨击“反科学”势力，并列出了代表性人物及作品；3段谈到科学的捍卫者在会议上表示了他们的担忧，而1段指出自然科学和人文学科之间的分歧在加深。由此可知，2、3段是一段的顺接和延伸，即其是对1段的进一步说明，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【细节干扰】A 讨论科学影响力下降的原因：2段2句虽提到：由于科研经费减少，科学家们开始著书来抨击“反科学”势力。但2、3段中仅此一处涉及科学界势力减弱的原因。可见A选项并非2、3段讨论的主要内容，更谈不上是其写作目的，故排除。

【过度推理】B 表示作者对科学家的同情：2、3段提到，科学影响力下降，科学家们不得不通过著作或会议来抨击“反科学”势力，但并没有相关信息显示出作者对科学家们表示同情，故B选项过度推理，故排除。

【无中生有】C 说明科学发展的方式：文中未提及科学发展的方式，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. Environmentalists were blamed for anti一science in an essay.

   环保主义者在一篇文章中被指责为反科学

B. Politicians are not subject to the labeling of anti一science.

   政治家不易被贴上反科学的标签

C.the “more enlightened” tend to tag others as anti一science.

   “更有见识的人”倾向于给别人贴反科学标签

D. Tagging environmentalists as “anti一science” is justifiable.

   把环保主义者称为“反科学”是合理的


【定位及答案】

6段2句提到：但这并不是说，那此环保主义者是反科学的，然而去年5月份刊登在《美国新闻和世界报导》的一篇文章却似乎暗示是这么回事。言下之音即《美国新闻和世界报导》的一篇文章暗示环保主义者是反科学的。A选项是对此的同义转述，故正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】B 政治家不易被贴上反科学的标签：5段提到反科学标签被贴到很多群体身上，从官方人士（authorities）到共和党人（Republicans）。显然内者均属于politicians，由此可知，反科学标签被贴到了政治家身上，故排除。

【过度推理】C “更有见识的人” 倾向于给别人贴反科学标签：8段3句指出反科学的共同之处，即“会激怒或威胁那些自以为比别人更有见识的人”，这说明“有见识的人”会因反科学而发怒，并不能由此推出他们鉴定别人为反科学故C选项属于过度推理，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 把环保主义者称为“反科学”是合理的：7段1句提到“环保主义者不可避免地会对这种批评作出回应”，言下之意为“给环保主义者贴反科学标签是不公平的”，而D选项表意与之相反，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. impartial    公平的

B. subjective    主观的

C. biased     有偏见的

D. puzzling     令人迷惑的


【定位及答案��

根据题干信息定位至全文。1段提到自然科学与人文学科之间的分歧越来越大，2、3段举例说明此现象。4至7段指出乱贴“反科学”标签的现象。8段指出观察者为“反科学”一词可能失去其意义而担忧。可见，作者并未直接表明自己的观点或态度，而是通过引用各方对科学与反科学的看法，全面地看待问题。因此作者对“科学与反科学之争”的态度是公正的、不偏不倚的，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】通过分析全文内容可知，作者只是引述各方观点，并未表明自己批判反科学，而B选项“主观的”、C选项“有偏见的”均为反向干扰，故排除。

【反向干扰&无中生有】D 令人迷惑的：文中作者引述了各方观点，全面地讨论了“科学与反科学之争”，所以作者的态度是公正的，而原文中并未提及与D选项相关的内容，故排除。

sections.passage:
1 Emerging from the 1980 census is the picture of a nation developing more and more regional competition, as population growth in the Northeast and Midwest reaches a near standstill.
1 This development — and its strong implications for US politics and economy in years ahead — has enthroned the South as America ’s most densely populated region for the first time in the history of the nation ’s head counting.
1 Altogether, the US population rose in the 1970s by 23.2 million people — numerically the third-largest growth ever recorded in a single decade. 2 Even so, that gain adds up to only 11.4 percent, lowest in American annual records except for the Depression years.
1 Americans have been migrating south and west in larger numbers since World War II, and the pattern still prevails.?
1 Three sun-belt states — Florida, Texas and California — together had nearly 10 million more people in 1980 than a decade earlier. 2 Among large cities, San Diego moved from 14th to 8th and San Antonio from 15th to 10th — with Cleveland and Washington,D.C., dropping out of thetop10.
1 Not all that shift can be attributed to the movement out of the snow belt, census officials say. 2 Nonstop waves of immigrants played a role, too — and so did bigger crops of babies as yesterday ’s “ baby boom ” generation reached its child-bearing years.
1 Moreover, demographers see the continuing shift south and west as joined by a related but newer phenomenon: More and more Americans apparently are looking not just for places with more jobs but with fewer people, too.? 2 Some instances —
1 Regionally, the Rocky Mountain states reported the most rapid growth rate — 37.1 percent since 1970 in a vast area with only 5 percent of the US population.
1 Among states, Nevada and Arizona grew fastest of all: 63.5 and 53.1 percent respectively.? 2 Except for Florida and Texas, thetop10 in rate of growth is composed of Western states with 7.5 million people — about 9 per square mile.
1 The flight from overcrowdedness affects the migration from snow belt to more bearable climates.
1 Nowhere do 1980 census statistics dramatize more the American search for spacious living than in the Far West.? 2 There, California added 3.7 million to its population in the 1970s, more than any other states.
1 In that decade, however, large numbers also migrated from California, mostly to other parts of the West. 2 Often they chose — and still are choosing — somewhat colder climates such as Oregon, Idaho and Alaska in order to escape smog, crime and other plagues of urbanization in the Golden State.
1 As a result, California’s growth rate dropped during the 1970s, to 18.5 percent -- little more than two thirds the 1960s’ growth figure and considerably below that of other Western states.

【定位及答案】

4段提到“自第二次世界大战以来，大量的美国人向南部和西部迁移”。言下之意��20世纪70年代也是美国人口向西南迁移的时期。题干的in 1970s对应四段的since World War Ⅱ，B选项中的southwestern shif4 of population是对3段中have been migrating south and west（向南部和西部迁移）的同义替换，故B选项正确。

    坚持旧生活方式的保守人士


【定位及答案】

6段提到人口普查官员发表了一些研究结果接着7段1句讲到demographers还从数据中发现了一种新的现象。这说明demographers也是从事人口普查工作的人。浏览选项可知，C选项符合此意，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 赞同民主倾向的人：选项是利用七段中的demographers和该选项中的democracy具有相同前缀demo一这一点编造出来的干扰项，且文中并未提及有关于democracy的任何话题，故排除。

【无中生有】B 倡导州际间移民的人：选项是根据文章出现频率较高的词汇migration（迁移），states（州）等编造出来的无关干扰项，故排除。

【无中生有】D 坚持旧生活方式的保守人士：选项原文未提及，属无中生有，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text5
sections.passage:
1 Scattered around the globe are more than 100 small regions of isolated volcanic activity known to geologists as hot spots. 2 Unlike most of the world ’s volcanoes, they are not always found at the boundaries of the great drifting plates that make up the earth ’s surface; on the contrary, many of them lie deep in the interior of a plate. 3 Most of the hot spots move only slowly, and in some cases the movement of the plates past them has left trails of dead volcanoes. 4 The hot spots and their volcanic trails are milestones that mark the passage of the plates.
1 That the plates are moving is now beyond dispute.? 2 Africa and South America, for example, are moving away from each other as new material is injected into the seafloor between them. 3 The complementary coastlines and certain geological features that seem to span the ocean are reminders of where the two continents were once joined.? 4 The relative motion of the plates carrying these continents has been constructed in detail, but the motion of one plate with respect to another cannot readily be translated into motion with respect to the earth ’s interior. 5 It is not possible to determine whether both continents are moving in opposite directions or whether one continent is stationary and the other is drifting away from it. 6 Hot spots, anchored in the deeper layers of the earth, provide the measuring instruments needed to resolve the question. 7 From an analysis of the hot-spot population it appears that the African plate is stationary and that it has not moved during the past 30 million years.
1 The significance of hot spots is not confined to their role as a frame of reference. 2 It now appears that they also have an important influence on the geophysical processes that propel the plates across the globe. 3 When a continental plate comes to rest over a hot spot, the material rising from deeper layers creates a broad dome. 4 As the dome grows, it develops deep fissures (cracks); in at least a few cases the continent may break entirely along some of these fissures, so that the hot spot initiates the formation of a new ocean.? 5 Thus just as earlier theories have explained the mobility of the continents, so hot spots may explain their mutability (inconstancy).?

【选项概览】

A. the motion of the plates corresponds to that of the earth's interior

   板块的运动与地球内部的运动

B. the geological theory about drifting plates has been proved to be true

   地质学上的板块漂移学说已被证明是正确的

C. the hot spots and the plates move slowly in opposite directions

   热点和板块朝相反的方向缓慢移动

D. the movement of hot spots proves the continents are moving apart

   热点的运动证明各大陆（即大陆板块）正在彼此分开


【定位及答案】

2段1句作者明确指出“板块谓移这理论现在是毋庸置疑的”，接着作者义以非洲和南美洲为例对这一观点进行说明，因此B选项与文意相符，其中drifting plate（板块漂移）同义替换了原文2段1句中的the plate are moving（板块漂移）；has been proved 1o be true（被证明是正确的）对应原文2段1句中的is now beyond dispute（现在是毋庸置疑的）故B选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 板块的运动与地球内部的运动：2段4句提到：板块间的相对运动不能被理解成是板块相对于地球内部的运动，而A选项表意与之相反，故排除。

【偷换概念】C 热点和板块朝相反的方向缓慢移动：1段3句虽提到大多数热点在缓慢地移……板块经过这些热点时会留下死火山的痕迹，但并未提及热点与板块之间的相对运动，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 热点的运动证明各大陆（即大陆板块）正在彼此分开：2段目句提到：��球深层的热点充当大陆板块相对运动的测量仪器，可见是热点本身证明了大陆的分离，而非热点的运动证明了此现象，故排除。

A. the two continents are still moving in opposite directions

D. over 100 hot spots are scattered all around the globe

   地球上散布着一百多个热点


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息Africa and South America可定位至2段2句。该句提到，非洲和南美洲之间的距离越来越远。但紧接着3句指出：相互吻合的海岸线和某些地质特征提醒我们，这两个大陆曾经是连在一起的。言下之意，具有相互吻合的海岸线和某些相同的地质特征是这两个大陆曾经连在一起的证据，故B选项正确。

【答非所问】2段7句指出：在过去的3000万年里非洲大陆没有移动过；1段1句提到：地球上散落分布着100多个热点。但这些都不是证明非洲和南美洲曾经相连的充分条件。故C、D两个选项错误。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. the structure of the African plates

    非洲板块的构造

B. the revival of dead volcanoes

    死火山的复活

C. the mobility of the continents

    大陆的移动性

D. the formation of new oceans

    新海洋的形成


【定位及答案】

题干的hot-spot theory和useful是对3段1句The significance of hot spots的同义替换。该段首先讲到：热点的重要性不仅局展于用作参照体系，它们还对板块漂移过程有着重要影响。接着3句具体说明了热点导致大陆反块断裂，进而形成新海洋的过程。因此，D选项是热点理论所能解释的内容故正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 非洲板块的构造：2段7句指出热点理论解释了非洲板块是静止不动的，但并未提到热点理论揭示了非洲板块的构造，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 死火山的复活：1段3句提到“板块经过这些热点时会留下死火山的痕迹”，但并未提及死火山的复活，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. the features of volcanic activities

    火山活动的特点

B. the importance of the theory about drifting plates

   板块漂移理论的重要性

C. the significance of hot spots in geophysical studies

    热点在地球物理学研究中的重要意义

D. the process of the formation of volcanoes

    火山的形成过程


【定位及答案】

1段介绍了热点的定义及其与板块之间的联系，2段讲到热点在板块移动的研究中提供参照作用，3段讲到热点对地球物理学过程的研究也有重要影响。综上，全文内容都是围绕“热点对地球物理学研究的重要意义”展开的。C选项是对全文内容的合理概括，故正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 火山活动的特点：1段1句提到的“火山活动区”是为了定义热点，并未描述火山活动，故A选项无中生有，故排除。

【断章取义】B 板块漂移理论的重要性：2段1句提到“板块漂移理论”，以引出5句“其不能证明的问题”，从而得出3段5句热点理论或许可以解释“大陆板块的易变性”。这说明热点理论才是本文讨论的重点，故排除。

【答非所问】D 火山的形成过程：1段3句提到“板块经过这些热点时会留下死火山的痕迹”，以解释热点的特点，可见火山的形成与文章主旨无关，故排除D选项。

sections.title: 翻译
sections.passage:
1 While there are almost as many definitions of history as there are historians, modern practice most closely conforms to one that sees history as the attempt to recreate and explain the significant events of the past.? 2 Caught in the web of its own time and place, each generation of historians determines anew what is significant for it in the past. 3 In this search the evidence found is always incomplete and scattered; it is also frequently partial or partisan. 4 The irony of the historian ’s craft is that its practitioners always know that their efforts are but contributions to an unending process.
1 Interest in historical methods has arisen less through external challenge to the validity of history as an intellectual discipline and more from internal quarrels among historians themselves.? 2 While history once revered its affinity to literature and philosophy, the emerging social sciences seemed to afford greater opportunities for asking new questions and providing rewarding approaches to an understanding of the past. 3 Social science methodologies had to be adapted to a discipline governed by the primacy of historical sources rather than the imperatives of the contemporary world. 4 During this transfer, traditional historical methods were augmented by additional methodologies designed to interpret the new forms of evidence in the historical study.?
1 Methodology is a term that remains inherently ambiguous in the historical profession. 2 There is no agreement whether methodology refers to the concepts peculiar to historical work in general or to the research techniques appropriate to the various branches of historical inquiry.? 3 Historians, especially those so blinded by their research interests that they have been accused of “ tunnel method,” frequently fall victim to the “ technicist fallacy ”. 4 Also common in the natural sciences, the technicist fallacy mistakenly identifies the discipline as a whole with certain parts of its technical implementation.
1 It applies equally to traditional historians who view history as only the external and internal criticism of sources, and to social science historians who equate their activity with specific techniques.?

questions.stem:
① 尽管关于历史的定义几乎和历史学家的数量一样多，但现代史学家的实践最接近这样一种定义，即认为历史学是试图重现并解释过去的重大史实的科学。② 由于受到自身时空的限制，每一代历史学家都要重新确定过去哪些重大事件对他们来说意义重大。③ 在这样的研究中，所发现的证据往往是不完整且零散的；而且这些证据常常带有片面性或倾向性。④历史学家这门手艺的讽刺之处在于，从事研究的人始终明白，他们所做的努力只不过是为一个永无止境的研究过程做一些贡献罢了。
① 人们对历史研究方法的兴趣，与其说是源于外部对历史学作为一门知识学科的合理性提出的质疑，不如说是源于历史学家内部之间的争论。② 尽管历史学在历史上曾因其与文学和哲学的密切联系而备受尊崇，但新兴的社会科学似乎为提出新问题以及为理解过去提供有价值的研究方法创造了更多机会。③ 社会科学方法论必须适应这样一个学科，其以历史资料为主导，而不是以当代社会规则的需要为主导。④ 在这一转变过程中，传统的历史研究方法得到了额外方法的补充，这些方法旨在解读历史研究中的新型证据形式。
① 在历史学领域，“方法论”这个术语本质上一直是模糊不清的。② 所谓的方法论指的是一般的历史研究中所特有的概念，还是指历史研究中各个具体领域所适用的研究手段，人们对此看法不一。③历史学家，尤其是那些因对自身研究兴趣太过执着、以至于被指责为采用“隧道式研究法”的人，常常会陷入“技术主义谬误”。④ 技术谬论错误地把某个学科整体与学科研究中所使用的部分技术操作方法等同起来，这种现象在自然科学领域也很普遍。
① 这种谬论同样存在于两类历史学家：一类是传统历史学家，他们将历史仅视为对史料的外部和内部考证；另一类是社会科学历史学家，他们将自身的研究活动等同于特定的研究方法。
questions.answer: 几乎每个历史学家对史学都有自己的定义，但现代史学家的实践最趋向于认为历史学是一门试图重现并解释过去重大史实的科学。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“While there are almost as many definitions of history as there are historians”，这部分是while引导的让步状语从句，almost意为“几乎”；as many definitions of history as是“as many +可数名词复数+as”的比较级结构，可译为“与...一样多”。这句话可以直译为“有多少历史学家，就有多少关于历史的定义”。“modern practice most closely conforms to one”modern practice的表面意思是“现代的实践”，但联系while引导的让步状语从句，此部分译为：但现代史学家的实践最趋向于，“that sees history as the attempt to recreate and explain the significant events of the past.”本部分为that引导的定语从句，修饰one，see history意为将历史学看作，由于修饰attempt的动词不定式短语to recreate and explain...过长，翻译attempt时可使用词性转换法，将其译为名词“...的重现和解释”。

【句子结构分析】

“During this transfer”为介词短语，是独立成分，可译为在这种转变中。“traditional historical methods were augmented ”本部分句子谓语使用了被动语态，翻译时转换为主动语态，译为...充实了...。“ traditional historical methods”为传统的历史研究方法，“by additional methodologies designed to interpret the new forms of evidence in the historical study.”，此部分，介词by后面的宾语是additional methodologies，表示新方法，过去分词短语designed作后置定语，翻译时译为旨在...的新方法，介词短语 in the historical study.作状语，与to interpret the new forms of evidence合译为阐释历史研究中的新证据。

questions.stem:
① 尽管关于历史的定义几乎和历史学家的数量一样多，但现代史学家的实践最接近这样一种定义，即认为历史学是试图重现并解释过去的重大史实的科学。② 由于受到自身时空的限制，每一代历史学家都要重新确定过去哪些重大事件对他们来说意义重大。③ 在这样的研究中，所发现的证据往往是不完整且零散的；而且这些证据常常带有片面性或倾向性。④历史学家这门手艺的讽刺之处在于，从事研究的人始终明白，他们所做的努力只不过是为一个永无止境的研究过程做一些贡献罢了。
① 人们对历史研究方法的兴趣，与其说是源于外部对历史学作为一门知识学科的合理性提出的质疑，不如说是源于历史学家内部之间的争论。② 尽管历史学在历史上曾因其与文学和哲学的密切联系而备受尊崇，但新兴的社会科学似乎为提出新问题以及为理解过去提供有价值的研究方法创造了更多机会。③ 社会科学方法论必须适应这样一个学科，其以历史资料为主导，而不是以当代社会规则的需要为主导。④ 在这一转变过程中，传统的历史研究方法得到了额外方法的补充，这些方法旨在解读历史研究中的新型证据形式。
① 在历史学领域，“方法论”这个术语本质上一直是模糊不清的。② 所谓的方法论指的是一般的历史研究中所特有的概念，还是指历史研究中各个具体领域所适用的研究手段，人们对此看法不一。③历史学家，尤其是那些因对自身研究兴趣太过执着、以至于被指责为采用“隧道式研究法”的人，常常会陷入“技术主义谬误”。④ 技术谬论错误地把某个学科整体与学科研究中所使用的部分技术操作方法等同起来，这种现象在自然科学领域也很普遍。
① 这种谬论同样存在于两类历史学家：一类是传统历史学家，他们将历史仅视为对史料的外部和内部考证；另一类是社会科学历史学家，他们将自身的研究活动等同于特定的研究方法。
questions.answer: 所谓的方法论指的是一般的历史研究中所特有的概念，还是指历史研究中各个具体领域所适用的研究手段，人们对此看法不一。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“There is no agreement”为存在句，no agreement译为没有一致的观点。“ whether methodology refers to the concepts peculiar to historical work in general”中methodology译为方法论，refers to可译为指的是，形容词短语peculiar to...作concepts的后置定语，译为一般的历史研究中所特有的概念。“ or to the research techniques appropriate to the various branches of historical inquiry. ”中，形容词短语appropriate to...作research techniques的后置定语，译为历史研究中各个具体领域适用的研究手段。

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“It applies equally to traditional historians ”直译为它同样适用于传统历史学家，但是，这里有两处需要改进，首先要说明it指代的内容，It指代前面提及的fallacy，译为这种谬论，其次，traditional historians中historians为复数，与后面 social science historians结构上相对应，翻译时可译为历史传统派和历史社科派，“who view history as only the external and internal criticism of sources”中，“external and internal criticism of ”可以理解为史学界外部和内部人士对...的评论。“ and to social science historians who equate their activity with specific techniques.”中social science historians 译为历史社科派，who引导定语从句，修饰social science historians ，equate...with意为把...等同，使相等。

sections.title: 完型填空
sections.passage:
1 Industrial safety does not just happen. 2 Companies 1 low accident rates plan their safety programs, work hard to organize them, and continue working to keep them 2 and active.? 3 When the work is well done, a 3 of accident-free operations is established 4 time lost due to injuries is kept at a minimum.?
1 Successful safety programs may 5 greatly in the emphasis placed on certain aspects of the program.? 2 Some place great emphasis on mechanical guarding.   3 Others stress safe work practices by 6 rules or regulations.   4 7 others depend on an emotional appeal to the worker.? 5 But, there are certain basic ideas that must be used in every program if maximum results are to be obtained.
1 There can be no question about the value of a safety program.   2 From a financial standpoint alone, safety 8.? 3 The fewer the injury 9, the better the workman's insurance rate.? 4 This may mean the difference between operating at 10 or at a loss.?

questions.explanation:
【答案解析】

从四个选项可知，空格处应填介词。分析句子结构可知，空格处所填介词应能与low accident rates搭配作Companies的后置定语。A选项at常与rate搭配，构成短语at a/the rate（of）意为“以……的速度/比率”，代入文中表示“低事故速度的公司”，显然与文意不符，况且该短语不能作定语修饰名词，故A选项予以排除。B、C选项均不能和rate搭配使用，故予以排除。D选项with意为“具有，带有”，用来表示附属于某一物品的某种显著特点，因此Companies with low accident rates意为“事故发生率低的公司”，符合上下文语义，故D选项正确。

【答案解析】

空格处所填词与and后的active构成并列关系，因此空格处所填词在语意和感情色彩上应与active保持一致，且与active可以一起修饰them（即safety programs安全措施）。A选项alive（有活力的）与active（活跃的）形似意近，且可以修饰safety programs，为正确选项。B选项vivid常用语描述画面真实生动，C选项mobile表示移动，二者均不能修饰safetyprograms，故予以排除。D选项diverse重点强调事物的多样性，与active表意无关，故排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句中含一When引导的条件状语从句，此从句已然为主句铺设了前提条件，即“如果上述工作（制定安全方案、组织实施这些方案，并使其保持活力和有效性）做得好，那么无事故操作的___就可以建立起来”。B选项climate意为“气氛，氛围”，代入文中，意为“建立起无事故的工作氛围”，既能承接上文，作为有效完成工作的结果，又是下文“工伤损失的时间会被控制在最低限度”的条件，故为正确答案。根据逻辑判断，建立无事故操作的“规章”和“要求”都不是可能出现的结果，故排除A、D两个选项。circumstance当作复数时，可以表示“环境”；作单数时，则表示“某种情况或特定事件”，C选项circumstance为单数，不能表本环境，因此予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格前后为完整独立的两个句子。联系上下文，判断出前者（a climate of accident-free operations is established）为后者（time lost due to injuries is kept at a minimum）的原因，也可看作是后者发生的前提条件。由此可知，空格处应填入连词、关系代词或关系副词。四个选项中，只有D选项unless为连词，意为“除非”，但是代入文中后，不符合逻辑，故排除。因此，空格处应填入关系代词或关系副词。A选项where为关系副词，可引导定语从句，修饰主语a climate，代入文中，表示“在这样一种无事故的工作氛围中，因工伤损失的时间会被控制在最低限度”，符合原文逻辑，为正确答案。how作为关系副词以及what作为关系代词都只能引导名词性从句，而不能引导定语从句，故B、C两个选项均予以排除。

【答案解析】

本题所在文章的第二段落为明显的总分结构，题目所在当句为二段总起句，是对其他分论点的总结。阅读后文中的分论点可知，成功的安全措施应该是将重点放在不同的方面，B选项的differ符合题意，为正确答案。A选项的alter不能与介词in搭配，故排除。C选项shift与in搭配，译为“在...中移动或改变位置”，带入文中语义不通，故排除。D选项distinguish译为“区分，不同”，常与between和from连用，不与介词in搭配，故排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句为Others stress safe work practices byrules or regulations，其中Others指代的是Other successful safety programs，by___表示方式或手段，因此该句意为“另一些成功的安全方案强调通过___规章制度来实施安全生产”。空格实际上考查的是动词与rules or regulations的搭配关系。C选项observing（遵守）与rules or regulations搭配时，表示“遵守规章制度”，符合文意，为正确选项。而A选项constituting（构成；成立）的宾语一般是组织机构实体；B选项aggravating（恶化；激怒）与rules or regulations搭配，显然不符合常识；D选项justifying（证明……正确）的宾语一般存在争议，而文中“规章制度”为正面的安全指导，并无争议，故都排除。

【答案解析】

结合2段2、3句可知，改句属于“Some......Others....Still others....”结构，本段首句提到，成功的安全方案在侧重点上大有不同，紧接着作者论述词观点：“Some......Others....___ others..."，由此可知，三个例子之间为并列关系，空格处应该填写连词或副词，D选项still表示“仍然，依然”，带入文中复合上下文之间的并列关系，且能够构成常用于表达举例的固定搭配，故为正确选项。A、B两个选项用在句中时，均不能与上文形成并列关系，故排除。C选项even表示递进关系，侧重强调后面的内容，不符合原文表达并列的逻辑关系，故排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句表示“仅从财政的角度来看，在安全生产上花钱是___”，由此可知，空格处所填词应与financial（财政）有关。此外，下文提到“工伤___越少，工人的保险费率就越低。”由此不难推知，安全生产意义重大，故而为此花钱是值得的。C选项pays off（值得，有回报）代入文中，意为“在安全生产上花钱是值得的”，符合上下文语义，为正确答案。A选项comes off（举行；发生）、B选项turns up（出现；到来）与D选项holds up（举起；保持）均与financial无关，且不能表达安全方案是有价值的，故都排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句位于“The fewer...,the better...”构成的反比关系中，因此空格处所填词应满足“伤害___越少”与“工人保险费率越高”的反比关系。四个选项中只有A选项claims（索赔）代入文中，可表示“工伤索赔越少，工人的保险费率就越高”这一反比关系，故A选项正确。其余三个选项分别表示“伤害报告“伤害声明”以及“伤害公告”，这显然不能表达出与工人保险费率之间的反比关系，故三者均予以排除。

【答案解析】

由于or表示一种选择关系，因此空格所在部分与at a loss语义相反，D选项at a profit表示“获利”，恰好与at a loss表意相反，为正确答案，A、B两个选项均不能与at搭配，故排除。C选项interest作名词时可表示利益，但只有做不可数名词时才能与介词at搭配表示“利息”，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text1
sections.passage:
1 It’s a rough world out there. 2 Step outside and you could break a leg slipping on your doormat. 3 Light up the stove and you could burn down the house. 4 Luckily, if the doormat or stove failed to warn of coming disaster, a successful lawsuit might compensate you for your troubles.
 5 Or so the thinking has gone since the early 1980s, when juries began holding more companies liable for their customers’ misfortunes.?
1 Feeling threatened, companies responded by writing ever-longer warning labels, trying to anticipate every possible accident.? 2 Today, stepladders carry labels several inches long that warn, among other things, that you might — surprise! — fall off. 3 The label on a child ’s Batman cape cautions that the toy “ does not enable user to fly.”
1 While warnings are often appropriate and necessary — the dangers of drug interactions, for example — and many are required by state or federal regulations, it isn’t clear that they actually protect the manufacturers and sellers from liability if a customer is injured. 2 About 50 percent of the companies lose when injured customers take them to court.
1 Now the tide appears to be turning. 2 As personal injury claims continue as before, some courts are beginning to side with defendants, especially in cases where a warning label probably wouldn’t have changed anything.? 3 In May, Julie Nimmons, president of Schutt Sports in Illinois, successfully fought a lawsuit involving a football player who was paralyzed in a game while wearing a Schutt helmet. 4 “ We’re really sorry he has become paralyzed, but helmets aren’t designed to prevent those kinds of injuries,” says Nimmons. 5 The jury agreed that the nature of the game, not the helmet, was the reason for the athlete’s injury. 6 At the same time, the American Law Institute — a group of judges, lawyers, and academics whose recommendations carry substantial weight — issued new guidelines for tort law stating that companies need not warn customers of obvious dangers or bombard them with a lengthy list of possible ones. 7 “ Important information can get buried in a sea of trivialities,” says a law professor at Cornell law School who helped draft the new guidelines. 8 If the moderate end of the legal community has its way, the information on products might actually be provided for the benefit of customers and not as protection against legal liability.?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. Customers might be relieved of their disasters through lawsuits.

   顾客可以通过法律诉讼免受灾难

B. Injured customers could expect protection from the legal system.

   受伤的顾客有望得到法律制度的保护

C. Companies would avoid being sued by providing new warnings.

   公司将会通过提供新的警示信息来避免被起诉

D. Juries tended to find fault with the compensations companies promised.

   陪审团倾向于对公司所承诺的赔偿找茬


【定位及答案】

由题干中的1980s定位至1段5句。该句指出，自1980s起，这种想法就已出现，那时陪审团让更多的公司对其顾客所遭受的不幸负责。这里的“这种想法”即4句提到的顾客遭受危害后通过诉讼可能得到赔偿。由此可知，在1980s，遭受危害的（即受伤的）顾客可能（即有望）得到法律保护，故B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 顾客可以通过法律诉讼免受灾难：1段4句提到遭到危害的顾客可以通过诉讼获得赔偿，而非A选项中的“免受灾难”，故排除。

【过度推理】C 公司将会通过提供新的警示信息来避免被起诉：由3段1句可知：发生事故后，警示信息能否使公司免责尚不清楚，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 陪审团倾向于对公司所承诺的赔偿找茬：由1段5句可知：陪审团让公司对其顾客所遭受的不幸负责，并非D选项所说的陪审团对公司所承诺的赔偿找茬，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. satisfy customers by writing long warnings on products

    通过在产品上写长长的警示信息来满足顾客

B. become honest in describing the inadequacies of their products

    在描述自已产品的不足上表现得诚实

C. make the best use of labels to avoid legal liability

    充分利用警告标识语来避免法律责任

D. feel obliged to view customers' safety as their first concern

    不得不将顾客的安全看作头等重要的事


【定位及答案】

由题干首先定位至2段1句。题干中的Manufacturers与该句中的companies所指相同，该句谈到companies（即Manufacturers）感觉处境受到威胁，便做出反应，写出尽量长的警示标识语。结合上文，这里的“受到威胁”即1段5句提到的陪审团让公司对顾客所遭受的不幸负责。可见，companies（即Manufacturers）充分利用警示标识语是为了免责，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】2段1句点明公司写长警示标识语的目的是预先提示顾客潜在的危险事故，而这一做法的目的是避免法律责任，而非A选项中的satisfy customers（满足顾客），B选项中的诚实面对自己产品的不足以及D选项的将顾客的安全看作头等重要的事，均是对文章2段1句内容的曲解。故A、B、D三个选项都予以排除。

questions.explanation:

A. some injury claims were no longer supported by law

B. helmets were not designed to prevent injuries

D.some sports games might lose popularity with athletes

    某些体育项目可能不再获得运动员的青睐


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Schutt helmet定位至4段。4段1句指出，这种趋势（即3段2句提到的被受到伤害的消费者告上法庭，约50%的公司会输掉官司）正在转变；2句指明具体的转变（即法庭开始支持被告）；接着通过舒特公司的头盔胜诉事件进行说明。由此可知，作者举这一例子是为了证明4段1、2句中提及的某些伤害索赔不再得到法律的支持这一现象，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【以例证例】B 设计头盔不是为了预防伤害：4段4句谈到，舒特公司总裁尼蒙斯辩解时提到头盔并非为了预防这类伤害（即瘫痪）而设计，B选项的不是为了预防伤害是例子本身，并非例子要说明的问题，故排除。

【无中生有】C 产品标签最终将不再被使用：文中并未提及产品标签最终会被废弃，故排除。

【无中生有】D 某些体育项目可能不再获得运动员的青睐：选项内容在文中无法找到任何对应信息，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. biased   有偏见的

B. indifferent   冷漠的

C. puzzling   令人迷惑的

D. objective   客观的


【定位及答案】

解答该题时，考生首先要明白题干中the issue的指代。纵观全文可知，the issue指个人伤害索赔案件问题。1至3段作者客观地叙述索赔案的由来、发展，紧接着在4段提到法庭对该类索赔案态度的转变。作者自始至终都是站在第三者的角度客观论述实际情况，文中并未体现作者任何感情色彩和偏向性的主观态度，由此不难看出，作者对这一问题的态度是不偏不倚的，即“客观的”，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 有偏见的：由上述分析可知，作者对索赔案的态度是客观的，并无个人偏见，A选项“有偏见的”与全文的论述基调相悖，故排除。

【反向干扰】B 冷漠的：选项“冷漠的”可直接排除，因为作者对某一问题或观点发表评论，恰好说明了作者是关注这一问题的，冷漠一说无从谈起。

【无中生有】C 令人迷惑的：选项“令人迷惑的”在原文中并无依据，故排除。

1 In the first year or so of Web business, most of the action has revolved around efforts to tap the consumer market.? 2 More recently, as the Web proved to be more than a fashion, companies have started to buy and sell products and services with one another. 3 Such business-to-business sales make sense because business people typically know what product they’re looking for.
1 Nonetheless, many companies still hesitate to use the Web because of doubts about its reliability. 2 “ Businesses need to feel they can trust the pathway between them and the supplier,” says senior analyst Blane Erwin of Forrester Research. 3 Some companies are limiting the risk by conducting online transactions only with established business partners who are given access to the company ’s private intranet.
1 Another major shift in the model for Internet commerce concerns the technology available for marketing. 2 Until recently, Internet marketing activities have focused on strategies to “ pull ” customers into sites. 3 In the past year, however, software companies have developed tools that allow companies to “ push ” information directly out to consumers, transmitting marketing messages directly to targeted customers. 4 Most notably, the Pointcast Network uses a screen saver to deliver a continually updated stream of news and advertisements to subscribers ’ computer monitors. 5 Subscribers can customize the information they want to receive and proceed directly to a company’s Website. 6 Companies such as Virtual Vineyards are already starting to use similar technologies to push messages to customers about special sales, product offerings, or other events. 7 But push technology has earned the contempt of many Web users. 8 Online culture thinks highly of the notion that the information flowing onto the screen comes there by specific request.? 9 Once commercial promotion begins to fill the screen uninvited, the distinction between the Web and television fades. 10 That’s a prospect that horrifies Net purists.?
1 But it is hardly inevitable that companies on the Web will need to resort to push strategies to make money. 2 The examples of Virtual Vineyards, Amazon.com, and other pioneers show that a Website selling the right kind of products with the right mix of interactivity, hospitality, and security will attract online customers.? 3 And the cost of computing power continues to free fall, which is a good sign for any enterprise setting up shop in silicon. 4 People looking back 5 or 10 years from now may well wonder why so few companies took the online plunge.

A. has been striving to expand its market

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the beginning of the passage和Web business可定位至1段。该段主要描述了网络商务的兴起，1句便开门见山点明：“在网上交易开始的第一年前后，大部分活动都围绕着努力开发消费者市场进行。”A选项中的has been striving和to expand its market分别是对1句中has revolved around efforts和to tap the consumer market的同义替换，故为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【词汇干扰】B 打算遵循一种空幻的时尚：1段3句虽提到a fashion，但B选项中的a fashion中添加了修饰限定词fanciful（幻想的），使得语义发生了变化，故排除。

【无中生有】C 企图控制市场，但徒劳无功：选项在文中并未提及，故排除。

A. the technology is popular with many Web users

【定位及答案】

由题干中的technology available for marketing可定位至3段。该段1、2、3句表明软件公司开发出了新的技术，使得网络营销策略实现了由“拉”向“推”的巨大转变，紧接着4、5、6句以Pointcast 网络和Virtual Vineyards公司对“推”技术的应用为例，具体说明了营销策略的这一变化。由“拉”向“推”属根本性的巨大转变，C选项中的radical change恰好符合此意，且C选项是对原文三段信息的合理推断，故为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 这种技术受到许多网络用户的欢迎：选项中提到的“the technology”究竟指“push”technology 还是“pull” technology ，并不清楚，若是前者，则与3段7句提到的“‘推’的技术遭到许多网络用户的鄙视”相悖，故排除。

【反向干扰】B 公司对在线交易的可靠性充满信心：2段1句提到，由于怀疑网络的可靠性，许多公司对是否使用网络举棋不定，B选项与此表述相悖，故排除。

【张冠李戴】D 这种技术仅限于对固定合作伙伴使用：2段3句提到，有些公司只向固定的贸易伙伴开放公司的内部局域网，并非只让他们使用营销的在线技术，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. there should be no marketing messages in online culture

    在线文化中不应该有营销信息

B. money making should be given priority to on the Web

    网络的首要目的是赚钱

C. the Web should be able to function as the television set

    网络的功能应与电视一样

D. there should be no online commercial information without requests

    未经要求就不应该提供在线商业信息


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Net purists可定位至3段10句。句仅给出结论：“这种前景让网络净化者惶恐不安”，因此解答该题的关键是联系上文语境，弄清“前景”一词的指代。9句提到：“一旦商业促销不请自来，充斥电脑屏幕，那么网络和电视之间的界线就模糊不清了”，这种情况便是1句描述的让网络净化者惶恐不安的前景，故由这两句的逻辑关系可反向推出：网络净化者不希望看到商业促销随意充斥在电脑屏幕上，即应该应特定需求提供在线的商业信息，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 在线文化中不应该有营销信息：根据3段9、10句可知，Net purists反对的是未经要求就提供在线商业信息的商业促销行为，而非“营销信息”本身，故排除。

【无中生有】B 网络的首要目的是赚钱：文中并未出现“网络的首要目的是赚钱”这一信息，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 网络的功能应与电视一样：文中3段9句提到，一旦商业促销未经要求就充斥电脑屏幕，那么网络和电视就没有多大差别了。由此可知，Net purists认为网络和电视的功能应存在差异，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text3
sections.passage:
1 An invisible border divides those arguing for computers in the classroom on the behalf of students ’ career prospects and those arguing for computers in the classroom for broader reasons of radical educational reform. 2 Very few writers on the subject have explored this distinction — indeed, contradiction — which goes to the heart of what is wrong with the campaign to put computers in the classroom.?
1 An education that aims at getting a student a certain kind of job is a technical education, justified for reasons radically different from why education is universally required by law. 2 It is not simply to raise everyone ’s job prospects that all children are legally required to attend school into their teens. 3 Rather, we have a certain conception of the American citizen, a character who is incomplete if he cannot competently assess how his livelihood and happiness are affected by things outside of himself. 4 But this was not always the case: before it was legally required for all children to attend school until a certain age, it was widely accepted that some were just not equipped by nature to pursue this kind of education. 5 With optimism characteristic of all industrialized countries, we came to accept that everyone is fit to be educated.? 6 Computer-education advocates forsake this optimistic notion for a pessimism that betrays their otherwise cheery outlook. 7 Banking on the confusion between educational and vocational reasons for bringing computers into schools, computer-ed advocates often emphasize the job prospects of graduates over their educational achievement.
1 There are some good arguments for a technical education given the right kind of student. 2 Many European schools introduce the concept of professional training early on in order to make sure children are properly equipped for the professions they want to join. 3 It is, however, presumptuous to insist that there will only be so many jobs for so many scientists, so many businessmen, so many accountants. 4 Besides, this is unlikely to produce the needed number of every kind of professional in a country as large as ours and where the economy is spread over so many states and involves so many international corporations.?
1 But, for a small group of students, professional training might be the way to go since well-developed skills, all other factors being equal, can be the difference between having a job and not. 2 Of course, the basics of using any computer these days are very simple. 3 It does not take a lifelong acquaintance to pick up various software programs. 4 If one wanted to become a computer engineer, that is, of course, an entirely different story. 5 Basic computer skills take — at the very longest — a couple of months to learn. 6 In any case, basic computer skills are only complementary to the host of real skills that are necessary to becoming any kind of professional.? 7 It should be observed, of course, that no school, vocational or not, is helped by a confusion over its purpose.

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. far-reaching   意义深远的 

B. dubiously oriented   目标不明确的

C. self-contradictory   自相矛盾的

D. radically reformatory   具有彻底改革性的 


【定位及答案】

由题干中的put computers in the classroom定位至1段。该段1句开门见山地指出：因将计算机引入课堂的不同目的（学生的就业前景1s.彻底的教育改革）而引发的分歧。紧接着2句作者便立刻总结：上述两种分歧之间的区别虽触及问题实质，却很少被探讨。可见，作者认为因目的不清而引发的分歧并未解决，即把计算机引人课堂这一做法的目标尚不明确，B选项是对该语义的合理推断，故正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 意义深远的：选项在文中并未提及，故排除。

【词汇干扰&答非所问】C 自相矛盾的：1段2句出现 contradiction一词，C选项是利用该词设置的派生词汇干扰，原文文意为将计算机引人课堂的两种目的是一对矛盾，而非将计算机引人课堂的做法自相矛盾，且self-contradictory一词一般用来形容两种事物之间自相矛盾，答非所问，故排除。

【答非所问】D 具有彻底改革性的：1段1句是说一些人提议将计算机引人课堂的目的是为了彻底的教育改革，而这并非作者对将计算机引人课堂这一现象的评价，故排除。

【选项概览】

A. dependent upon the starting age of candidates

    取决于学员开始接受培训的年龄 

B. worth trying in various social sections

    值得在社会各界尝试

D. attractive to every kind of professional

    吸引各种专业人员


【定位及答案】

由题干中的European model of professional training定位至3段2句。该句指出：“欧洲的许多学校很早就引进了职业培训的概念。”4句则指出，在我们……国家里，……这样做（即采用职业培训模式）不可能培养出所需数量的各种专业人才。显然，作者认为：在其所在的国家，欧洲职业培训模式并不可行（即没有实际价值）故C选项正确。

sections.title: 阅读Text4
sections.passage:
1 When a Scottish research team startled the world by revealing 3 months ago that it had cloned an adult sheep, President Clinton moved swiftly. 2 Declaring that he was opposed to using this unusual animal husbandry technique to clone humans, he ordered that federal funds not be used for such an experiment — although no one had proposed to do so — and asked an independent panel of experts chaired by Princeton President Harold Shapiro to report back to the White House in 90 days with recommendations for a national policy on human cloning.? 3 That group -- the National Bioethics Advisory Commission (NBAC) -- has been working feverishly to put its wisdom on paper, and at a meeting on 17 May, members agreed on a near-final draft of their recommendations.
1 NBAC will ask that Clinton ’s 90-day ban on federal funds for human cloning be extended indefinitely, and possibly that it be made law. 2 But NBAC members are planning to word the recommendation narrowly to avoid new restrictions on research that involves the cloning of human DNA or cells — routine in molecular biology. 3 The panel has not yet reached agreement on a crucial question, however, whether to recommend legislation that would make it a crime for private funding to be used for human cloning.?
1 In a draft preface to the recommendations, discussed at the 17 May meeting, Shapiro suggested that the panel had found a broad consensus that it would be “ morally unacceptable to attempt to create a human child by adult nuclear cloning.” 2 Shapiro explained during the meeting that the moral doubt stems mainly from fears about the risk to the health of the child. 3 The panel then informally accepted several general conclusions, although some details have not been settled.
1 NBAC plans to call for a continued ban on federal government funding for any attempt to clone body cell nuclei to create a child. 2 Because current federal law already forbids the use of federal funds to create embryos (the earliest stage of human offspring before birth) for research or to knowingly endanger an embryo ’s life, NBAC will remain silent on embryo research.?
1 NBAC members also indicated that they will appeal to privately funded researchers and clinics not to try to clone humans by body cell nuclear transfer. 2 But they were divided on whether to go further by calling for a federal law that would impose a complete ban on human cloning. 3 Shapiro and most members favored an appeal for such legislation, but in a phone interview, he said this issue was still “ up in the air.”?

A. federal funds have been used in a project to clone humans

B. the White House responded strongly to the news of cloning

C. NBAC was authorized to control the misuse of cloning technique

D. the White House has got the panel's recommendations on cloning

    白宫已得到专家小组关于克隆技术的建议


【定位及答案】

由题干定位至1段。该段1句通过苏格兰成功克隆绵羊这事件引出话题——克隆技术，接着2句点明以克林顿总统为首的白宫强烈反对该技术用于克隆人类，下令禁止联邦资金用于此类实验，并成立专家小组责令其拿出有关克隆人的国策建议。显然，由moved swiftly（迅速地作出反应）、Declaring（宣布）、ordered（命令）和asked（要求）不难看出，白宫对克隆这一消息表示强烈反对，故B选项为正确答案。


【错���分析】

【反向干扰】A 联邦资金已被用于一项克隆人的计划中：1段2句提到白宫下令禁止使用联邦资金克隆人类，并成立专家小组责令其拿出有关克隆人的国策建议，故排除。

【过度推理】C NBAC被授权控制克隆技术的误用：1段2句中提到的是NBAC被要求提出建议，并没有被授权控制克隆技术的误用，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 白宫已得到专家小组关于克隆技术的建议：1段2句仅可获悉克林顿总统对专家小组提出要求，但专家小组还未给出建议，且文章后面相关时态（般将来时）也印证了这一点，故排除。

A. embryo research is just a current development of cloning

由题干中的embryo定位至4段2句。仔细分析该句及题干发现：2句中的remain silent实际上就是题干中的leave…undiscussed的同义再现：2句和题干均为复合句，其从句均为because引导的原因状语从句，不同之处在：2句为先因后果，题干则先果后因。因此，我们可以此为突破口进行解题。试者将4段2句顺序颠倒为题干的先果后因：NBAC将在这一问题上保持沉默（即题干的“不再讨论胚胎研究问题”），因为联邦法律已禁止使用联邦基金去制造供研究用的胚胎或故意危及胚胎生命。浏览备选项，D选项中的explicitly stated and settled in the law是对该句中current federal law already forbids 的同义转述，故正确。

【偷换概念】C 胚胎的生命在胚胎研究中不会受到威胁：4段2句提到禁止故意危及胚胎的生命的行为，由此推知，胚胎的生命在胚胎研究中可能会受到威胁，故排除。

A. some NBAC members hesitate to ban human cloning completely

    有些NBAC委员对全面禁止克隆人持犹豫的态度

B. a law banning human cloning is to be passed in no time

sections.title: 阅读Text5
sections.passage:
1 Science, in practice, depends far less on the experiments it prepares than on the preparedness of the minds of the men who watch the experiments.? 2 Sir Isaac Newton supposedly discovered gravity through the fall of an apple. 3 Apples had been falling in many places for centuries and thousands of people had seen them fall. 4 But Newton for years had been curious about the cause of the orbital motion of the moon and planets. 5 What kept them in place? 6 Why didn’t they fall out of the sky? 7 The fact that the apple fell down toward the earth and not up into the tree answered the question he had been asking himself about those larger fruits of the heavens, the moon and the planets.
1 How many men would have considered the possibility of an apple falling up into the tree? 2 Newton did because he was not trying to predict anything. 3 He was just wondering. 4 His mind was ready for the unpredictable. 5 Unpredictability is part of the essential nature of research. 6 If you don’t have unpredictable things, you don’t have research. 7 Scientists tend to forget this when writing their cut and dried reports for the technical journals, but history is filled with examples of it.?
1 In talking to some scientists, particularly younger ones, you might gather the impression that they find the “ scientific method ” a substitute for imaginative thought.? 2 I’ve attended research conferences where a scientist has been asked what he thinks about the advisability of continuing a certain experiment. 3 The scientist has frowned, looked at the graphs, and said “ the data are still inconclusive.” 4 “ We know that,” the men from the budget office have said, “ but what do you think? 5 Is it worthwhile going on? 6 " What do you think we might expect?” 7 The scientist has been shocked at having even been asked to speculate.
1 What this amounts to, of course, is that the scientist has become the victim of his own writings. 2 He has put forward unquestioned claims so consistently that he not only believes them himself, but has convinced industrial and business management that they are true. 3 If experiments are planned and carried out according to plan as faithfully as the reports in the science journals indicate, then it is perfectly logical for management to expect research to produce results measurable in dollars and cents.? 4 It is entirely reasonable for auditors to believe that scientists who know exactly where they are going and how they will get there should not be distracted by the necessity of keeping one eye on the cash register while the other eye is on the microscope. 5 Nor, if regularity and conformity to a standard pattern are as desirable to the scientist as the writing of his papers would appear to reflect, is management to be blamed for discriminating against the “ odd balls ” among researchers in favor of more conventional thinkers who “work well with the team.”

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. inquiring minds are more important than scientific experiments

    爱探索的头脑比科学实验更重要

B. science advances when fruitful researches are conducted

    当进行的研究有成果时，科学就会有所进步

C. scientists seldom forget the essential nature of. Research

    科学家很少会忘记研究的基本特征

D. unpredictability weighs less than prediction in scientific research

    科学研究中，不可预测性没有可预测性重要


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Isaac Newton定位至1段2句。 该句举出牛顿通过观察苹果落地而发现万有引力的事例来论证本文论点，故本题解题的关键在于对文章论点（即1句）的理解。仔细分析该句发现，句中的far less… than…句型含明显的比较意义一否定前者，肯定后者，故论点强调的是有所准备的头脑远比事先准备好的实验重要。浏览备选项，发现A选项是对该句的同义转述，故正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】B 当进行的研究有成果时，科学就会有所进步：选项内容在文中并未提及，故排除。

【偷换概念】C 科学家很少会忘记研究的基本特征：选项把原文2段7句中的tend to forget（往往会忘记）偷换成seldom forget（很少会忘记），而且该句也不是作者引用牛顿的例子想要证明的内容，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 科学研究中，不可预测性没有可预测性重要：选项与2段5句（不可预测性是研究不可或缺的一一个基本特征）语义相悖，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. shouldn't replace “scientific method” with imaginative thought

    不应该用想象思维代替“科学方法”

B. shouldn't neglect to speculate on unpredictable things

    不应该忽视推断不可预测之事

C. should write more concise reports for technical journals

    应该为科技期刊撰写更简明的报告

D. should be confident about their research findings

    应该对自己的研究发现有自信


【定位及答案】

由题干中的scientists 首先定位至2段7句。该句仅给出结论：科学家们撰写论文时往往会忘记this。因此解答此题的关键是联系上下文语境，弄清this指代的内容。2段5、6句的内容均在强调不可预测性作为研究不可或缺的基本特征，意义重大，由此推知，不可预测性即为7句所提到的this，故由这两句的逻辑关系反推出科学家们撰写论文时不应该忘记研究的不可预测性，B选项是对此的合理推断，故正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 不应该用想象思维代替“科学方法”：文章3段举例说明：希望科学家不要用“科学方法”代替想象思维，故排除。

【无中生有】选项C和D内容在文中均未提及，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. have a keen interest in prediction

    对预测十分感兴趣

B. often speculate on the future

    经常预测未来

C. think highly of creative thinking

    对创造性思维高度重视

D. stick to“scientific method"

    坚信“科学方法”


【定位及答案】

由题干中的young scientists定位至3段1句，句中的younger ones即some young scientists。作者在该句指出“年轻科学家认为‘科学方法’可以替代想象思维”，并举例对此予以详细说明。由此可见，比起想象思维，年轻科学家更偏向于“科学方法”，D选项是对该句的同义转述，故正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】C 对创造性思维高度重视：3段1句表明年轻科学家认为“科学方法”可以替代想象思维。由此可知，年轻科学家并不重视创造性思维，C选项与之相悖，故排除。

【词汇干扰】举例说明中，3段7句指出：这位科学家没有料到人们会让他做出预测，由此可推知年轻科学家对预测并不感兴趣，预测未来一说更无从谈起，故A选项和B选项仅是根据7句中的speculate设置的词汇干扰，故排除A、B。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. may not be as profitable as they are expected

    可能不像预期的那样有利可图

B. can be measured in dollars and can cents

    可以用金钱来衡量

C. rely on conformity to a standard pattern

    依赖于与某种标准模式的致性

D. are mostly underestimated by management

    大多数都被管理层低估了


【定位及答案】

由题干中的关键信息the results of scientific research定位到4段3句。该句用If条件状语从句假设了一种情况：如果实验像科学杂志报告中表明的那样照计划不折不扣地去设计和完成那么对管理层来说，期待研究能够产生用金钱衡量的成果是完全符合逻辑的。言下之意是，科学实验中总是会存在一些难以预测的现象，因此不能肯定地说某项实验必定会产生经济效益。A选项是对原文的合理推断，故正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】B选项和C选项分别属于4段3句和5句中If假设情况下的结果和条件，所表达的意义需要加上从句和主句才完整。单从选项表意来看，其都与文章表述相悖，事实上并不成立，故排除。

大多数都被管理层低估了

sections.title: 翻译
sections.passage:
1 Governments throughout the world act on the assumption that the welfare of their people depends largely on the economic strength and wealth of the community. 2 Under modern conditions, this requires varying measures of centralized control and hence the help of specialized scientists such as economists and operational research experts.? 3 Furthermore, it is obvious that the strength of a country ’s economy is directly bound up with the efficiency of its agriculture and industry, and that this in turn rests upon the efforts of scientists and technologists of all kinds.? 4 It also means that governments are increasingly compelled to interfere in these sectors in order to step up production and ensure that it is utilized to the best advantage. 5 For example, they may encourage research in various ways, including the setting up of their own research centers; they may alter the structure of education, or interfere in order to reduce the wastage of natural resources or tap resources hitherto unexploited; or they may cooperate directly in the growing number of international projects related to science, economics and industry. 6 In any case, all such interventions are heavily dependent on scientific advice and also scientific and technological manpower of all kinds.
1 Owing to the remarkable development in mass-communications, people everywhere are feeling new wants and are being exposed to new customs and ideas, while governments are often forced to introduce still further innovations for the reasons given above.? 2 At the same time, the normal rate of social change throughout the world is taking place at a vastly accelerated speed compared with the past. 3 For example, in the early industrialized countries of Europe the process of industrialization — with all the far-reaching changes in social patterns that followed — was spread over nearly a century, whereas nowadays a developing nation may undergo the same process in a decade or so.? 4 All this has the effect of building up unusual pressures and tensions within the community and consequently presents serious problems for the governments concerned. 5 Additional social stresses may also occur because of the population explosion or problems arising from mass migration movements — themselves made relatively easy nowadays by modern means of transport.? 6 As a result of all these factors, governments are becoming increasingly dependent on biologists and social scientists for planning the appropriate programs and putting them into effect.

questions.stem:
① 世界各国政府都基于这样一种假设行政，那就是人民的福利在很大程度上取决于本国的经济实力和社会财富。② 在现代条件下，这就需要采取不同的中央调控措施，从而就需要获得诸如经济学和运筹学领域的专家的协助。③ 而且，显而易见的是，一个国家的经济实力与其工农业的生产效率直接相关，而效率的提高则又依赖于各类科技人员的努力。④ 这也意味着：政府必须逐步加大对这些行业的干预力度，以便提高产量，确保其发挥最佳效益。⑤ 例如，政府可以鼓励利用各种方法进行科学研究，包括建立自己的研究中心；政府还可以转变教育结构，或是进行干预，以减少自然资源的浪费和开发至今尚未利用的资源；政府还可以在日益增多的与科学、经济和工业有关的跨国项目中直接开展合作。⑥ 无论如何，所有这些干预都极度依赖于科学的建议，同时也依赖于各类科技人才的力量。
① 大众传媒的显著发展使各地的人们不断感到有新的需求，并不断接触到新习俗和新观念，同时，由于上述原因，政府也常常被迫推行更进一步的革新措施。② 与此同时，与过去相比，世界各地社会变化的常规进程正在以飞快的速度大幅度发展。③ 比如，在早先实现工业化的欧洲国家中，其工业化进程以及随之而来的各种影响深远的社会结构变革，持续了近一个世纪之久，而如今一个发展中国家在十年左右就可能完成这个过程。④ 这一切所带来的后果是加大了社会内部异乎寻常的压迫感和紧张感，从而给有关政府提出了若干严重的问题。⑤ 由于人口爆炸或大规模移民运动引发的问题，可能还会产生额外的社会压力——而现代交通工具使得大规模移民运动如今相对容易进行。⑥ 正因为所有的这些因素，��府变得越来越依赖生物学家和社会学家制定的合理计划，并将它们付诸实践。

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“Under modern conditions, this requires varying measures of centralized control ”中Under modern conditions为状语，译为在现代条件下，this为主语，指代上句内容，可不译出，仅译为这，measure作为不可数名词，意为程度，作为可数名词且常以复数形式出现，意为措施、办法，因此居中varying measures译为不同的措施，作requires的宾语。of centralized control为后置定语，翻译时可置于被修饰词measures之前，译为集中控制措施，即这部分整理为“在现代条件下，这需要不同的集中控制措施”。“and hence the help of specialized scientists ”中the help为requires的第二个宾语，of specialized scientists作help的后置定语，可译为专业科学家的帮助，根据搭配和表达习惯，翻译时需要增译动词获得，故译为从而获得专业科学家的帮助。“ such as economists and operational research experts. ”中operational research experts为术语意为运筹学专家。

sections.title: 完型填空
sections.passage: 1 If a farmer wishes to succeed, he must try to keep a wide gap between his consumption and his production.   2 He must store a large quantity of grain 1 consuming all his grain immediately.? 3 He can continue to support himself and his family 2 he produces a surplus.? 4 He must use this surplus in three ways: as seed for sowing, as an insurance 3 the unpredictable effects of bad weather and as a commodity which he must sell in order to 4 old agricultural implements and obtain chemical fertilizers to 5 the soil.? 5 He may also need money to construct irrigation 6 and improve his farm in other ways.? 6 If no surplus is available, a farmer cannot be 7.? 7 He must either sell some of his property or 8 extra funds in the form of loans.? 8 Naturally he will try to borrow money at a low 9 of interest, but loans of this kind are not 10 obtainable.?

questions.explanation:
【答案解析】

文章首句指出，农民要成功，必须保持其粮食消耗和生产之间的巨大差距，换言之即其粮食生产量应远远高于其消耗量，这就需要store a large quantity of grain（储存大量粮食），而空格后的做法consuming all his grain immediately（立即消耗其全部粮食）显然不可取。由此可知，空格所在句表达“应该储存粮食而不能立即消耗”之意，可见，空格前后为对立关系，故空格处需填入一个表示转折关系的逻辑连接词。备选项中只有C选项instead of（而不是；代替）符合此要求，故正确。A选项other than（除……以外）表递进，B选项as well as（也，同）表并列，D选项more than（多过……）表比较，均不符合文章的逻辑要求，故都予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格前后的内容分别是：他可以继续养家糊口；他生产的粮食（除消耗外）有剩余。分析其间关系可知，后者是前者的前提条件或原因。备选项中只有A选项only if（只有）能够表示条件，符合这两句间的逻辑关系，故正确。B选项much as（虽然，尽管）一般表示转折或让步；C选项long before（早在……以前）和D选项ever since（自从……）均表示时间。三者都不符合两个句子间的逻辑关系，故都予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句主要说明储存余粮的三个目的：as seed...，as an insurance...和as a commodity...。空格所处部分即为目的之二，而分析空格后的the unpredictable effects of bad weather（坏天气带来的无法预测的后果）与an insurance（保障）之间的关系可知，储存粮食应是为了防止坏天气带来的无法预测的后果的一种保障。B选项against有“预防，防备”之意，符合句意，为正确答案。A、C两个选项分别与insurance搭配：insurance for（为……买保险）和insurance of（……的保险/保险额度）显然都与句意不符；此外，insurance不能与towards搭配，故排除A、C、D三个选项。

【答案解析】

空格所在句谈及储存余粮的三大目的，其中第三个目的又包含两方面： 旧农具以及购买化肥。由句中的并列连词and可知，空格所填词应与old agricultural implements构成动宾搭配；且通过分析and之后的内容可知，obtain chemical fertilizers可以帮助农民取得成功，因而old agricultural implements也应具有类似作用。备选项中只有A选项replace（更换，置换）符合此要求，故为正确答案。B选项purchase（采购）和C选项supplement（补充）代入原文后，均不合常理；D选项dispose常与of搭配构成dispose of（处理掉），且文中侧重以旧换新，而非仅停留在处理旧农具上，故这三个选项均排除。

【答案解析】

分析句子结构可知，obtain chemical fertilizers（购买化肥）的目的是___the soil（___土壤）。根据常识，化肥与土壤之间的关系只能是：化肥“滋养”土壤。C选项feed（饲养，喂）可引申为“滋养某事物”，故为正确答案。A选项enhance提高；加强）和D选项raise（种植；抚育）一般都不和soil搭配；B选项mix（混合）是利用人们对施肥过程的认知设置的干扰项，此处重在强调购买化肥的目的，所以排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句中，and连接的construct irrigation____与improve his farm in other ways构成并列关系，故前后所表达意思应一致。由空格后“以其他方式改善农田”可知，空格前的“修建灌溉____”也应是改善农田的方式之一。根据常识，与灌溉相关且需修建的应该是水渠、渠道等，因此空格所填词应与此相关。D选项channels（水渠；渠道）可与名词irrigation（灌溉）构成合理搭配，故正确。A选项vessels（器皿；船；血管），B选项routes（路线；航线）和C选项paths（小路，路径），都不能和irrigation搭配，均予以排除。

【答案解析】

本文显然是总分结构。文章首句即点明农民储存余粮具有重要性，文章前半部分从正面论述储存余粮的重要性，空格所在句从反面论述这一重要性。因此，本题所在句与42题所在句“有余粮才能继续养家糊口”相对应。由此可推断，本题所在句意为：没有余粮，农民就不能养活自己与家人。B选项self-suffident（自给自足的）与support himself and his family（养家糊口）意思相近，故为正确答案。A选项self-confident（自信的）、C选项self-satisfied（自满的，自负的）和D选项self-restrained（自我克制的）代入文中后，虽都能表明有余粮所导致的心态，但都不能与前文形成对照，故都排除。

【答案解析】

该句中，either...or...连接两种并列的措施：一是变卖家产；二是以贷款形式____额外的资金。通过分析可知，变卖家产可帮助农民获取资金，从而解决上文提到的“余粮不足”的问题，因此____extra funds in the form of loans也应有此作用，D选项seek与funds搭配，意为“筹集资金”，符合要求且与后一句中的“borrow money”相呼应，故为正确答案。A选项search（搜查）和B选项save（节约；保护）均与原文语境不符；C选项0加（提供）与文章意思互相矛盾，故都予以排除

【答案解析】

空格所在处谈到borrow money at a low___of interest（以低的利息___贷款），谈到贷款利息，自然使人联想到利率，而“利率”地道的英语表达是rate of interest或interest rate，故C选项rate（率）为正确答案。A选项proportion（比例）、B选项percentage（百分比）和D选项ratio（比率；比值）均与文章语境不符，都应排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句为but连接的并列句，but表明其前后语义存在转折关系。分句一提到“试图以低利息贷款”，分句二指出“这种低息贷款不是___能得到的”，因此判断，分句二应表示“不能或不可得到这种低息贷款”。只有D选项frequently（频繁地；通常地）符合句意，故正确。A选项genuinely（真正地；纯粹地）、B选项obviously（明显地）和C选项presumably（大概，或许）均与文意不符，都应排除。

sections.passage:
1 These two pictures display a sharp contrast: there were a lot of fish with one fishing boat in the sea in 1900 while the situation was just the opposite in 1995. 【图画描述：整体+细节对比】 2 Obviously, the fishing industry was facing a major problem, with all the ocean resources being exhausted so quickly. 【解释现象：海洋资源快速枯竭】
1 The author is not exaggerating or joking about commercial fishing. 【解释作者的写作目的1：没有夸大商业捕鱼】 2 On the contrary, he is seriously warning us that our way of thinking and ways of doing things are unreasonable and dangerous. 【解释作者的写作目的2：提出警示】 3 Our resources are limited and our ecosystem needs careful consideration and protection. 【正面论证1：资源有限，生态需要保护】 4 If we only care about the present, we will suffer in the future. 【反面论证1：只考虑现在的后果】 5 It’s just like building friendship and saving money: the more you put into it, the more you can get; the more you take out, the less it is left. 【举例类比2：用友情类比当前行为对未来的影响】
1 Measures should be taken if such disappointing situation is to be avoided. 【承上启下，引出建议】 2 I suggest that government make laws and regulations to guide and supervise people’s fishing activity, punishing those who only care about their own interest and bring harm to others and the environment. 【建议1：政府立法】 3 I also appeal to the public that money is not the only thing we can pursue and fish is not the only food we can eat. 【建议2：呼吁公众关注】 4 Whether for the benefit of the human race or for the interest of our own, we should show concern for others and make plans for the future. 【递进：呼吁为未来做好规划】 5 Only in this way can we live happily and affluently. 【展望未来】

sections.title: 阅读Text1
sections.passage:
1 A history of long and effortless success can be a dreadful handicap, but, if properly handled, it may become a driving force. 2 When the United States entered just such a glowing period after the end of the Second World War, it had a market eight times larger than any competitor, giving its industries unparalleled economies of scale.? 3 Its scientists were the world ’s best, its workers the most skilled. 4 America and Americans were prosperous beyond the dreams of the Europeans and Asians whose economies the war had destroyed.
1 It was inevitable that this primacy should have narrowed as other countries grew richer. 2 Just as inevitably, the retreat from predominance proved painful. 3 By the mid-1980s Americans had found themselves at a loss over their fading industrial competitiveness. 4 Some huge American industries, such as consumer electronics, had shrunk or vanished in the face of foreign competition. 5 By 1987 there was only one American television maker left, Zenith. 6 (Now there is none: Zenith was bought by South Korea’s LG Electronics in July.)? 7 Foreign-made cars and textiles were sweeping into the domestic market. 8 America’s machine-tool industry was on the ropes. 9 For a while it looked as though the making of semiconductors, which America had invented and which sat at the heart of the new computer age, was going to be the next casualty.
1 All of this caused a crisis of confidence. 2 Americans stopped taking prosperity for granted. 3 They began to believe that their way of doing business was failing, and that their incomes would therefore shortly begin to fall as well. 4 The mid-1980s brought one inquiry after another into the causes of America’s industrial decline. 5 Their sometimes sensational findings were filled with warnings about the growing competition from overseas.
1 How things have changed! 2 In 1995 the United States can look back on five years of solid growth while Japan has been struggling. 3 Few Americans attribute this solely to such obvious causes as a devalued dollar or the turning of the business cycle. 4 Self-doubt has yielded to blind pride.? 5 “ American industry has changed its structure, has gone on a diet, has learnt to be more quick-witted,” according to Richard Cavanagh, executive dean of Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government. 6 “ It makes me proud to be an American just to see how our businesses are improving their productivity,” says Stephen Moore of the Cato Institute, a think-tank in Washington, DC. 7 And William Sahlman of the Harvard Business School believes that people will look back on this period as “a golden age of business management in the United States.”?
