questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following can be inferred from the last paragraph？

从最后一段中可以推知一下哪个内容？

A. Vanity has more often been found in idealists.

   理想主义者往往比较虚荣

B. The fast-fashion industry ignores sustainability.

   快时尚产业忽略了可持续性

C. People are more interested in unaffordable garments.

   人们对买不起的衣服逬感兴趣

D. Pricing is vital to environment-friendly purchasing.

   价格对于环境友好型消费至关重要


【定位及答案】

由题干中的last paragraphs位在最后一段，文章最后一句说“虚荣之心人皆有之；只有在买不起很多东西的时候，人们才会开始可持续性购物”。D选项是对这句话的合理推断，即价格是进行环保型购物的变要因素，其中的Pricing（价格）对应afford，environment-friendly（环保的）对应sustainably，purchasing对应shopping，故为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【过度推理】A 理想主义者往往比较虚荣：6段3句提到了“虚荣之心人皆有之”，但没说在理想主义者身上很常见，故排除。

【反向干扰】B 快时尚产业忽略了可持续性：6段1句提到几家快时尚公司已经在努力控制其对劳工和环境的影响，这说明快时尚产业已经在关注自身的可持续性发展，B选项的表述与此相悖，故排除。

【无中生有】C  人们对买不起的衣服逬感兴趣：文中并未提及人们对哪类衣服更感兴趣，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

What is the subject of the text？

这篇文章的主题是什么？

A. Satire on an extravagant lifestyle.

   讽刺奢侈的生活方式

B. Challenge to a high-fashion myth.

   挑战高端时尚的神话

C. Criticism of the fast-fashion industry.

   批判快时尚产业

D. Exposure of a mass-market secret.

   暴露大众市场的秘密


【定位及答案】

从全文脉络来看，1段以一部电影为例，引出时尚这一话题；2段承接1段，点明本文核心内容——快时尚，并阐明克莱因对快时尚的批判态度及其对时尚业的危害；3至4段继续以批判的视角揭示出快时尚的弊端，如消耗自然资源、导致浪费等。第5、6段是继批判之后给出的解决措施。可见，批判快时尚产业是本文论述的核心，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【过度推理】A 讽刺奢侈的生活方式：选项推理过度，文章指出了快时尚的一些弊端，但并没有讽刺奢侈的生活方式，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 挑战高端时尚的神话：选项曲解文意，high fashion出现在首段中，是文中的一个例子，而非文章的主旨，故排除。

【以偏概全】D 暴露大众市场的秘密：该选项是作者在论证快时尚的危害时用到的一个论据，不是本文主题，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text2
sections.passage:
1 An old saying has it that half of all advertising budgets are wasted — the trouble is, no one knows which half. 2 In the internet age, at least in theory, this fraction can be much reduced. 3 By watching what people search for, click on and say online, companies can aim " behavioural " ads at those most likely to buy.?
1 In the past couple of weeks a quarrel has illustrated the value to advertisers of such fine-grained information: Should advertisers assume that people are happy to be tracked and sent behavioural ads? 2 Or should they have explicit permission?
1 In December 2010 America's Federal Trade Commission (FTC) proposed adding a "do not track" (DNT) option to internet browsers, so that users could tell advertisers that they did not want to be followed. 2 Microsoft 's Internet Explorer and Apple 's Safari both offer DNT; Google's Chrome is due to do so this year. 3 In February the FTC and the Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) agreed that the industry would get cracking on responding to DNT requests.?
1 On May 31st Microsoft set off the row. 2 It said that Internet Explorer 10, the version due to appear with Windows8, would have DNT as a default.
1 Advertisers are horrified. 2 Human nature being what it is, most people stick with default settings. 3 Few switch DNT on now, but if tracking is off it will stay off. 4 Bob Liodice, the chief executive of the Association of National Advertisers, says consumers will be worse off if the industry cannot collect information about their preferences.? 5 People will not get fewer ads, he says. 6 "They'll get less meaningful, less targeted ads."
1 It is not yet clear how advertisers will respond. 2 Getting a DNT signal does not oblige anyone to stop tracking, although some companies have promised to do so. 3 Unable to tell whether someone really objects to behavioural ads or whether they are sticking with Microsoft ’s default, some may ignore a DNT signal and press on anyway.?
1 Also unclear is why Microsoft has gone it alone. 2 After all, it has an ad business too, which it says will comply with DNT requests, though it is still working out how. 3 If it is trying to upset Google, which relies almost wholly on advertising, it has chosen an indirect method: there is no guarantee that DNT by default will become the norm. 4 DNT does not seem an obviously huge selling point for Windows8 — though the firm has compared some of its other products favourably with Google 's on that count before. 5 Brendon Lynch, Microsoft 's chief privacy officer, blogged:" We believe consumers should have more control." 6 Could it really be that simple??

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

It is suggested in Paragraph 1 that“behavioural”ads help advertisers to______ .

第一段表明，“行为”广告有助于广告商们_______.

A. ease competition among themselves

   缓解他们之间的竞争

B. lower their operational costs

   降低运营成本

C. avoid complaints from consumers

   避免消费者的投诉

D. provide better online services

   提供更好的在线服务


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Paragraph 1可定位在1段。该段1句指出半数广告预算被浪费；2句话锋一转，指出在网络时代，浪费现象可以得到改善；3句紧随其后，道出改善方法——通过投放“行为”广告来锁定最可能购买的人权。由此可见，“行为”广告的出现避免了广告商无针对性，广撒网式的广告推送行为，减少了他们的广告预算，从而帮助其降低运营成本。B选项的表述与此相符，故正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A和D两个选项在文中均未提及，属于无中生有，故排除。

【偷换概念】C 避免消费者的投诉：文中1段3句提到“企业能将‘行为’广告锁定在最可能购买的人群身上”，但未说明该行为能避免消费者的投诉，因此C选项错误。

【题目及选项概览】

“The industry”(Line 6, Para3) refers to______ .

“the industry”（该行业，3段4行）指的是____.

A. online advertise

   网上广告商

B. e-commerce conductors

   电子商务运营商

C. digital information analysts

   数字信息分析员

D. internet browser developers

   因特网浏览器开发商


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息可定位在3段。题干中的“The industry”出现在3段3句，要知其意，可结合上下文进行判断。该段1句先说建议在网络浏览器上添加“不跟踪”选项；2句又说微软的IE浏览器，苹果的Safari浏览器和谷歌浏览器先后提供“不跟踪”功能。由此可知，与“不跟踪”功能息息相关的是因特网浏览器开发商。所以3句中将会对“不跟踪”要求作出回应的the industry应该也是因特网浏览器开发商，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【答非所问】A 网上广告商：虽然3段1句有提到advertisers，意为：用户就可以告知广告商自己不希望被跟踪，但其并非本段中谈论的核心；而且需要回应DNT功能有最直接关系的是因特网浏览器开发商，而不是广告商，故排除。

【无中生有】B、C两个选项原文未提，属于无中生有。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Bob Liodice holds that setting DNT as a   default______ .

Bob Liodice 认为将“禁止追踪”设为默认状态______.

A. may cut the number of junk ads

   可能减少垃圾广告的数量

B. fails to affect the ad industry

   不会影响广告行业

C. will not benefit consumers

   消费者不会获益

D. goes against human nature

   违反了人类本性


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Bob Liodice可定位在5段。该段3句提到，如果“跟踪”默认关闭，即将“不跟踪”设为默认程序，浏览器就会一直处于“不跟踪”状态。4句紧随其后，道出这种做法带来的后果，即浏览器处于“不跟踪”状态会使本行业无法获知消费者的喜好，从而使消费者的情况变得更糟。既然是令消费者的情况变糟，那么消费者就不会从中获益，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 可能减少垃圾广告的数量：5段5、6句说人们接触到的广告不会减少，且这些广告将会更没有意义和针对性，故排除。

【反向干扰】B 不会影响广告行业：5段1句说广告商很恐慌，可见对广告行业的冲击会很大，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 违反了人类本性：利用5段2句中的Human nature设置干扰，该句只说“大多数用户都会坚持浏览器默认设置，人的本性就是这样”，并未提及将“不跟踪”设为默认程序违反了人类本性，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following is true according to Paragraph 6？

根据第六段，以下哪一个选项是正确的？

A. DNT may not serve its intended purpose.

   “不跟踪”可能无法实现其预期的目的

B. Advertisers are willing to implement DNT.

   广告商愿意实施“不跟踪”

C. DNT is losing its popularity among consumers.

   “不跟踪”在消费者中失去青睐

D. Advertisers are obliged to offer behavioural ads.

   广告商被迫提供行为广告


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息可定位在6段。该段2句表示，“不跟踪”信号无法迫使任何人停止跟踪；3句又进一步指出一些公司忽略“不跟踪”信号，继续跟踪用户的行为。由此可知，“不跟踪”无法阻止任何人或公司获取新关消费者喜好的信息，因此达不到它预期的目的，故A选项是正确答案。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】B 广告商愿意实施“不跟踪”：6段1句提及“广告商对此如何回应，现在还不得而知”，可见，广告商是否愿意实施“不跟踪”尚不可知，故排除。

【无中生有】C  “不跟踪”在消费者中失去青睐：选项在原文中没有提到，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 广告商被迫提供行为广告：利用6段3句中的behavioural ads设置干扰。分析一段内容可知，“行为”广告有助于锁定最可能购买的人群，从而避免无针对性的广告推送行为，为广告商缩减广告预算，所以他们应该是乐意，而非被迫提供行为广告，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

The author’s attitude towards what Brendon Lynch said in his blog is one of ______ .

作者对于Brendon Lynch在他的博客中所说的话的态度是_____.

A.indulgence   纵容

B.understanding    理解

C.appreciation    欣赏

D.skepticism     怀疑


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Brendon Lynch可定位在7段。该段5句提到Brendon Lynch在博客中表示用户应该拥有更多控制权；6句中作者立即对该言论进行了反问，即Could it really be that simple（但事情真的那么简单吗）？由此可见，作者对布兰登·林奇的观点表示怀疑，因此D选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 纵容：选项在原文中没有提及，故排除。

【反向干扰】根据上述分析可知，作者对Brendon Lynch的言论持怀疑态度，故不可能对其表示理解和欣赏，B、C两个选项错误，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text3
sections.passage:
1 Up until a few decades ago, our visions of the future were largely — though by no means uniformly — glowingly positive. 2 Science and technology would cure all the ills of humanity, leading to lives of fulfillment and opportunity for all.?
1 Now utopia has grown unfashionable, as we have gained a deeper appreciation of the range of threats facing us, from asteroid strike to epidemic flu and to climate change. 2 You might even be tempted to assume that humanity has little future to look forward to.
1 But such gloominess is misplaced. 2 The fossil record shows that many species have endured for millions of years — so why shouldn't we? 3 Take a broader look at our species' place in the universe, and it becomes clear that we have an excellent chance of surviving for tens, if not hundreds, of thousands of years. 4 Look up Homo sapiens in the " Red List " of threatened species of the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and you will read: " Listed as Least Concern as the species is very widely distributed, adaptable, currently increasing, and there are no major threats resulting in an overall population decline."?
1 So what does our deep future hold? 2 A growing number of researchers and organisations are now thinking seriously about that question. 3 For example, the Long Now Foundation has as its flagship project a mechanical clock that is designed to still be marking time thousands of years hence.
1 Perhaps willfully, it may be easier to think about such lengthy timescales than about the more immediate future.? 2 The potential evolution of today 's technology, and its social consequences, is dazzlingly complicated, and it's perhaps best left to science fiction writers and futurologists to explore the many possibilities we can envisage. 3 That's one reason why we have launched Arc, a new publication dedicated to the near future.
1 But take a longer view and there is a surprising amount that we can say with considerable assurance. 2 As so often, the past holds the key to the future: we have now identified enough of the long-term patterns shaping the history of the planet, and our species, to make evidence-based forecasts about the situations in which our descendants will find themselves.?
1 This long perspective makes the pessimistic view of our prospects seem more likely to be a passing fad. 2 To be sure, the future is not all rosy. 3 But we are now knowledgeable enough to reduce many of the risks that threatened the existence of earlier humans, and to improve the lot of those to come.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Our vision of the future used to be inspired by______ .

过去，我们对于未来的想象由_______激发。

A. our desire for lives of fulfillment

   我们对生活满足感的渴望

B. our faith in science and technology

   我们对科技的信心

C. our awareness of potential risks

   我们对潜在威胁的认识

D. our belief in equal opportunity

   我们对平等机会的信念


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Our vision of the future可定位到1段1句，该句总述过去我们对未来感到glowingly positive。2句紧接着说，科技能治愈人类所有疾病，使所有人过上充实且充满机遇的生活，这无疑显露出人们对科技持有的巨大信心，而这也正是人们对未来感到glowingly positive的原因。可见，我们对未来的憧憬受自身对科技有信心的启发，故B选项正确。


【错选分析】

【因果倒置】A选项和D选项都是因果倒置，lives of fulfillment以及opportunity都是科技带来的结果，并非原因。

【反向干扰】C 我们对潜在威胁的认识：2段1句说：随着我们对自己面临的威胁……有了更深入���了解，现在这种乌托邦式的理想已经不再流行。由此可知，对未来的憧憬不仅不会受对潜在威胁认识的启发，反而会因为这种认识而不复存在，故排除C选项。

【题目及选项概览】

The IUCN’s “Red List” suggests that human being are______ .

世界自然保护联盟《濒危物种红色名录》表明人类是_______.

A. a sustained species

   可以持久生存的物种

B. a threat to the environment

   对环境的一种威胁

C. the world’s dominant power

   世界的主宰力量

D. a misplaced race

   错位的种族


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的the IUCN’s “Red List”可定位至3段4句。该句在描述“智人”，即人类时，用到了very widely distributed，adaptable，currently increasing，no major threats以及Listed as Least Concern等系列表述。由此不难看出，人类具有分布广泛、适应能力强、数量不断增长、无主要威胁等优势，且被列为“无危物种”，这足以说明人类并无灭绝的风险，可以持久生存，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【细节干扰】B 对环境的一种威胁：3段4句提到“不存在导致整个物种（人类）数量减少的主要威胁”，而非说人类是“对环境的一种威胁”，故排除。

【无中生有】C 世界的主宰力量：选项原文没有提到，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 错位的种族：3段1句的misplaced用于形容悲观的想法，而非人类，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following is true according to Paragraph 5？

根据第5段，以下哪项是正确的？

A. Arc helps limit the scope of futurological studies.

   《弧线》帮助限定了未来学研究的范围

B. Technology offers solutions to social problems.

   技术为社会问题提供解决方法

C. The interest in science fiction is on the rise.

   人们对科幻小说的兴趣在增加

D. Our immediate future is hard to conceive.

   即将到来的未来很难设想


【定位及答案】

由题干中的Paragraph 5可定位在5段。该段1句指出“与思考即将到来的未来相比，思考如此之长的时间跨度似乎更为容易”，即思考即将到来的未来要比思考长时间跨度的将来更难，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 《弧线》帮助限定了未来学研究的范围：5段3句是说《弧线》致力于研究不久的将来，但并没有提到它能帮助限定未来学研究的范围，因此A选项属于曲解文意。

【偷换概念】B 技术为社会问题提供解决方法：5段2句提到由技术带来的社会影响复杂到难以形容，而非技术提供解决社会问题的方法，B选项亦为曲解文意。

【词汇干扰】C 人们对科幻小说的兴趣在增加：该句虽然也提到了science fiction，但并未提及人们对它的兴趣在增加，C选项属于词汇干扰。

choices.label: B
choices.text: adopt an optimistic view of the world

choices.label: C
choices.text: draw on our experience from the past

choices.label: D
choices.text: curb our ambition to reshape history

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

To ensure the future of mankind，it is crucial to ______ .

为了保证人类的未来，关键是要______。

A. explore our planet's abundant resources

   勘察地球的丰富资源

B. adopt an optimistic view of the world

   拥有积极的世界观

C. draw on our experience from the past

   从过去汲取经验

D. curb our ambition to reshape history

   抑制我们要改造历史的野心


【定位及答案】

根据题干信总可定位在6段，题干中的crucial对应6段2句中的the key，可在该句中寻找与本题相关的信息。分析该句可知，过去是打开未来之门的钥匙，识别出形成星球和人类历史的长期模式有助于预测子孙后代的未来，这说明从过去的发展模式中总结经验能为预测未来提供依据。由此可见，从过去汲取经验对人类未来至关重要，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 勘察地球的丰富资源：选项在原文中没有提及，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 拥有积极的世界观：1段提到人类对未来感到glowingly positive，且相信所有人都能过上充实且充满机遇的生活，但这不能等同于拥有积极的世界观，而且这也不是确保人类未来的关键，故排除。

【断章取义】D 抑制我们要改造历史的野心：该选项片面性地摘录了6段2句shaping the history的信息，属于断章取义。

【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following would be the best title for the text？

以下几个是本文最佳的标题？

A. Uncertainty about Our Future

   关于未来的不确定性

B. Evolution of the Human Species

   人类的进化

C. The Ever-bright Prospects of Mankind

   人类前途一片光明

D. Science，Technology and Humanity

   科学、技术和人类


【定位及答案】

文章1、2段先是指出过去人们对未来的憧憬十分美好，而如今对其不抱希望。但三段紧随其后，对这种悲观想法进行反驳，并辅以有力论据证明人类生存的可持续性。四至六段论述人们对未来的研究。末段强调我们掌握的知识足以降低威胁早期人类生存的风险，并改善未来的风险。可见，作者对人类未来十分看好，即认为人类前途是光明的，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 关于未来的不确定性：6段明确表示人类能预测到的事情多得惊人，如果能识别形成星球和人类历史的长期模式就能预测后代的未来，这足以说明我们对未来有把握，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 人类的进化：3段3、4句只对人类这一物种的特点和现状进行了描述，与人类的进化史无关，更不是文章的主题，故排除。

【以偏概全】D 科学、技术和人类：1段和5段虽提及科技和人类，但并非本文主要讨论的对象，故排除。

sections.passage:
1 On a five to three vote, the Supreme Court knocked out much of Arizona ’s immigration law Monday — a modest policy victory for the Obama Administration. 2 But on the more important matter of the Constitution, the decision was an 8-0 defeat for the Administration ’s effort to upset the balance of power between the federal government and the states.
1 In Arizona v. United States, the majority overturned three of the four contested provisions of Arizona’s controversial plan to have state and local police enforce federal immigration law. 2 The Constitutional principles that Washington alone has the power to "establish a uniform Rule of Naturalization" and that federal laws precede state laws are noncontroversial. 3 Arizona had attempted to fashion state policies that ran parallel to the existing federal ones.?
1 Justice Anthony Kennedy, joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the Court ’s liberals, ruled that the state flew too close to the federal sun. 2 On the overturned provisions the majority held that Congress had deliberately "occupied the field" and Arizona had thus intruded on the federal ’s privileged powers.
1 However, the Justices said that Arizona police would be allowed to verify the legal status of people who come in contact with law enforcement. 2 That’s because Congress has always envisioned joint federal-state immigration enforcement and explicitly encourages state officers to share information and cooperate with federal colleagues.?
1 Two of the three objecting Justice — Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas — agreed with this Constitutional logic but disagreed about which Arizona rules conflicted with the federal statute. 2 The only major objection came from Justice Antonin Scalia, who offered an even more robust defense of state privileges going back to the Alien and Sedition Acts.?
1 The 8-0 objection to President Obama turns on what Justice Samuel Alito describes in his objection as " a shocking assertion of federal executive power ". 2 The White House argued that Arizona’s laws conflicted with its enforcement priorities, even if state laws complied with federal statutes to the letter. 3 In effect, the White House claimed that it could invalidate any otherwise legitimate state law that it disagrees with.?
1 Some powers do belong exclusively to the federal government, and control of citizenship and the borders is among them. 2 But if Congress wanted to prevent states from using their own resources to check immigration status, it could. 3 It never did so. 4 The Administration was in essence asserting that because it didn’t want to carry out Congress ’s immigration wishes, no state should be allowed to do so either. 5 Every Justice rightly rejected this remarkable claim.?

questions.explanation:
【题目选项概览】

Three provisions of Arizona’s plan were overturned because they______ .

亚利桑那州方案中的三项条款被推翻，原因在于它们_____。

A. deprived the federal police of Constitutional powers

   剥夺了联邦警察执行宪法的权利

B. disturbed the power balance between different states

   打破了各州间的权利平衡

C. overstepped the authority of federal immigration law

   逾越了联邦移民法的权威

D. contradicted both the federal and state policies

   与联邦政策和州政策产生了冲突


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Three provisions of Arizona’s plan可定位在2段。2段1句首先点出亚利桑那州关于移民法的计划中有三项条款被推翻，紧接着2、3句便道出了被推翻的原因：宪法规定只有华盛顿有权“建立统一的入籍准则”且联邦法律高于州级法律，而亚利桑那州却试图制定与现有联邦法并行的州法，这显然违背了宪法的规定，也挑战了联邦移民法的权威，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】B 打破了各州间的权利平衡：选项利用1段2句设置干扰，该句的to upset the balance of power between the federal government and the states作Administration’s effort的后置定语，是说“奥巴马政府在打破联邦政府与各州间权力平衡问题上所做的努力”，而非亚利桑那州计划中的三项法律条款打破了各州间的权利平衡。

【无中生有】A选项和D选项在原文中没有提到，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Federal officers’ duty to withhold immigrants’ information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: States’ independence from federal immigration law.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

On which of the following did the Justices agree, according to Paragraph 4？

由第四段可知，大法官认可下列哪项内容?

A. Federal officers’ duty to withhold immigrants’ information.

   联邦官员有隐瞒移民信息的义务

B. States’ independence from federal immigration law.

   各州独立于联邦移民法

C. States’ legitimate role immigration enforcement.

   在移民法执行问题上各州的合法地位

D. Congress’s intervention in immigration enforcement.

   在移民法执行中国会的干涉权


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的paragraph 4可定位在4段。该段1句提到，大法官们认为亚利桑那州的警察有权对涉及法律执行事项之人进行身份核查，2句揭示了他们这么认为的原因：国会一贯想让联邦和州政府联合实施移民法，这就意味着各州在移民法执行上享有合法地位。既然1句中大法官们的想法是基于2句中国会的意愿，那这些法官必然会同意各州在移民法执行上享有合法地位，故C选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】4段2句中明确表示国会希望联邦和州政府联合实施移民法，并鼓励这些官员在实施移民法时共享信息，由此可见，各州不能独立于联邦移民法，联邦官员也不该隐瞒移民信息，故A、B两个选项均错误。

【无中生有】D 在移民法执行中国会的干涉权：选项在原文中没有提及，属于无中生有。

choices.label: D
choices.text: stood in favor of the states

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

It can be inferred from Paragraph 5 that the Alien and Sedition Acts______ .

从第五段可以推知,《外国人和煽动叛乱法案》______ 。

A. violated the Constitution

   违反了宪法

B. undermined the states’ interests

   损害了州的利益

C. supported the federal statute

   支持联邦法

D. stood in favor of the states

   维护州的利益


【定位及答案】

根据题干关键信息Paragraph 5和the Alien and Sedition Acts（《客籍法和惩治叛乱法》）可定位在5段2句。分析该句可知，安东尼·斯卡利亚大法官极力捍卫州特权，且这些特权可追溯到《客籍法和惩治叛乱法》，可见，《客籍法和惩治叛乱法》也是捍卫州特权，即维护州利益的，故D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 违反了宪法：选项原文未提，故排除。

【反向干扰】B 损害了州的利益：根据上述分析可知，《客籍法和惩治叛乱法》是维护州利益的，B选项的表述与此相悖，故排除。

【词汇干扰】C 支持联邦法：选项利用5段1句中的federal statute设置干扰，文中只说《客籍法和惩治叛乱法》维护州利益，并未提及其对联邦法支持与否。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The White House claims that its power of enforcement______ .

白宫宣称其执法权______。

A. outweighs that held by the states

   优先于各州

B. is dependent on the states’ support

   依赖于各州的支持

C. is established by federal statutes

   由联邦法律确认

D. rarely goes against state laws

   很少与州法律相违背


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息The White House可定位在6段。该段2句中先说白宫认为亚利桑那州的法律与联邦法的执法优先权相抵触，3句中又说白宫可以使自己不认可的任何州法律无效。由此可见，白宫的执法权力优先于各州，故A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】B 依赖于各州的支持：选项信息在原文没有提到，故排除。

【无中生有】C 由联邦法律确认：选项诚于常识干扰，因为人们普遍认为，政府的权利是联邦法律所赋予的，而文中并没有提到此类信息。

【断章取义】D 很少与州法律相违背：6段2句中提到...state laws complied with federal statutes...，该句的完整意思是即使州法律和联邦法完全一致，两者的执法优先权也是相矛盾的，D选项片面地摘录了complied with这一信息，故排除。

choices.text: Immigration issues are usually decided by Congress.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Justices intended to check the power of the Administration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Justices wanted to strengthen its coordination with Congress.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Administration is dominant over immigration issues.

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What can be learned from the last paragraph？

从最后一段可以了解到什么?

A. Immigration issues are usually decided by Congress.

   移民问题通常由国会决定

B. Justices intended to check the power of the Administration.

   大法官打算限制政府的权利

C. Justices wanted to strengthen its coordination with Congress.

   大法官们想要加强和国会的合作

D. The Administration is dominant over immigration issues.

   政府在移民问题上有主导权


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的the last paragraph可定位至7段。该段4句指出联邦政府认为只要自己不实施国会关于移民的诉求，各州也不被允许这么做。5句点明每位大法官对此的态度：均反对（rightly rejected）这种异乎寻常的主张，可见，他们想通过一致反对来对联邦政府施加限制。B选项的表述与此相符，故正确。


【错选分析】

【过度推理】A 移民问题通常由国会决定：7段2句只说国会有权阻止州政府核查移民身份，但不能推知移民问题是由国会决定的，故排除。

【过度推理】C 大法官们想要加强和国会的合作：7段虽提到了法官和国会，却没有提到双方是否有合作，故排除。

【偷换概念】D 政府在移民问题上有主导权：7段2、3、4句可知，国会与联邦政府在移民问题上有同等的权力，只是前者并未使用这种权力，而联邦政府所谓的主导权是其一厢情愿的想法，并非事实，故D选项错误。

sections.title: 翻译
sections.passage:
1 Music means different things to different people and sometimes even different things to the same person at different moments of his life. 2 It might be poetic, philosophical, sensual, or mathematical, but in any case it must, in my view, have something to do with the soul of the human being. 3 Hence it is metaphysical; but the means of expression is purely and exclusively physical: sound. 4 I believe it is precisely this permanent coexistence of metaphysical message through physical means that is the strength of music. 5 It is also the reason why when we try to describe music with words, all we can do is articulate our reactions to it, and not grasp music itself.?
1 Beethoven ’s importance in music has been principally defined by the revolutionary nature of his compositions. 2 He freed music from hitherto prevailing conventions of harmony and structure. 3 Sometimes I feel in his late works a will to break all signs of continuity. 4 The music is abrupt and seemingly disconnected, as in the last piano sonata. 5 In musical expression, he did not feel restrained by the weight of convention. 6 By all accounts he was a freethinking person, and a courageous one, and I find courage an essential quality for the understanding, let alone the performance, of his works.?
1 This courageous attitude in fact becomes a requirement for the performers of Beethoven ’s music. 2 His compositions demand the performer to show courage, for example in the use of dynamics. 3 Beethoven ’s habit of increasing the volume with an extreme intensity and then abruptly following it with a sudden soft passage was only rarely used by composers before him.?
1 Beethoven was a deeply political man in the broadest sense of the word. 2 He was not interested in daily politics, but concerned with questions of moral behavior and the larger questions of right and wrong affecting the entire society. 3 Especially significant was his view of freedom, which, for him, was associated with the rights and responsibilities of the individual: he advocated freedom of thought and of personal expression.?
1 Beethoven ’s music tends to move from chaos to order as if order were an imperative of human existence. 2 For him, order does not result from forgetting or ignoring the disorders that plague our existence; order is a necessary development, an improvement that may lead to the Greek ideal of spiritual elevation. 3 It is not by chance that the Funeral March is not the last movement of the Eroica Symphony, but the second, so that suffering does not have the last word. 4 One could interpret much of the work of Beethoven by saying that suffering is inevitable, but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.?

questions.stem:
① 音乐对不同的人来说意义不同，有时甚至对同一个人来说，在他生命的不同时期也有不同意义。② 音乐也许是诗意的、哲学的、感官的或精确的，但在我看来，不管怎样，音乐一定关乎人类的灵魂。③ 因此音乐是超自然的，然而音乐的表达方式却完完全全是有形的：声音。④ 我认为，恰恰是这种通过有形的物质载体去传递无形的精神内涵的永久共存方式，铸就了音乐的力量。⑤ 这也解释了为什么当我们试图用语言描述音乐的时候，充其量只能是说清楚自己的感受，而无法抓住音乐本身。
①贝多芬在音乐上的重要性主要体现在其作品的革命性方面。②他将音乐从至今依然流行的和声与结构常规中解放了出来。③ 从他晚期的作品中，我有时能够感受到一种想要打破一切连贯性符号的决心。④正如他的最后一首钢琴奏鸣曲那样，他的晚期曲作中常有遽然骤变，且似乎没有连贯性。⑤在音乐表达方面，他并未受到传统观念的限制。⑥总而言之，贝多芬是个思想自由且勇敢无畏的人，而且我认为勇气是理解、更是演奏其作品必不可少的品质。
①这种勇敢的态度实际上成了演奏贝多芬音乐作品的一个必要条件。②他的作品要求演奏者展现出勇气，例如在力度的运用方面。③ 贝多芬习惯以极强的力度来提高音量，随后突然转为轻柔的乐段，在他之前很少有作曲家这样做。
①从最广义上来说，贝多芬是一个热衷政治的人。②他对日常政治不感兴趣，但很关心道德行为问题以及影响整个社会的大是大非问题。③ 极具重要意义的是他的自由观，对他而言，自由与个人的权利和责任息息相关:他倡导思想自由和个人言论自由。
① 贝多芬的音乐往往会从混沌转向有序，仿佛秩序是人类生存的必需品。② 对他来说，遗忘或忽略那些困扰我们生存的混乱并不能带来秩序；秩序是一种必要的发展，是一种可能带来希腊理想中精神升华的进步。③《葬礼进行曲》没有成为《英雄交响曲》的最后乐章，而是第二乐章，这并非偶然，因为这样痛苦就不会成为最后的结局。④我们可以这样解读贝多芬的诸多作品：苦难是不可避免的，但是与苦难抗争的勇气使生活有了意义。
questions.answer: 这也是为什么当我们尝试用语言来描述音乐时，我们所能做的只是清楚地表达对音乐的感受，却不能领会音乐的本质。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

本句开头It is also the reason为一个完整的主+系+表结构，后面why引导的定语从句修饰the reason，放前面翻译，also表示前后句语义上更进一步，译为“也，还”即这也是为什么当我们尝试用语言来描述音乐时，“all we can do is articulate our reactions to it,”这部分考查了“all we can do is+(to)动词原形即我们能做的是/我们所能做的是，and连接的并列表语，“and not （to）grasp music itself.”grasp的本义为“抓住，掌握”但这里与music连用，则表示为“理解，领会”的意思，即可翻译为不能领会音乐的本质。

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

本句是由and连接的并列句，By all accounts为插入语即人们一致认为，，分句 “I（主） find（谓） courage （宾语）an essential quality for the understanding, let alone the performance, of hisworks.（宾语补足语）”介词短语for the understanding作quality的后置定语，注意quality的本义是“质量”但这里做可数名词，是“特征，品质”的意思。即这一品质，是理解其作品的关键，of his work作后置定语修饰由let alone连接的并列成分the understanding与the performance.即更是演奏其作品的关键。

①贝多芬在音乐上的重要性主要体现在其作品的革命性方面。②他将音乐从至今依然流行的和声与结构常规中解放了出来。③ 从他晚期的作品中，我有时能够感受到一种想要打破一切连贯性符号的决心。④正如他的最后一首钢琴奏鸣曲那样，他的晚期曲作中常有遽然骤变，且似乎没有连贯性。⑤在音乐表达方面，他并未受到传统观念的限制。⑥总而言之，贝多芬是个思想自由且勇敢无畏的人，而且我认为勇气是理解、更是演奏其作品必不可少的品质。
①这种勇敢的态度实际上成了演奏贝多芬音乐作品的一个必要条件。②他的作品要求演奏者展现出勇气，例如在力度的运用方面。③ 贝多芬习惯以极强的力度来提高音量，随后突然转为轻柔的乐段，在他之前很少有作曲家这样做。
①从最广义上来说，贝多芬是一个热衷政治的人。②他对日常政治不感兴趣，但很关心道德行为问题以及影响整个社会的大是大非问题。③ 极具重要意义的是他的自由观，对他而言，自由与个人的权利和责任息息相关:他倡导思想自由和个人言论自由。
① 贝多芬的音乐往往会从混沌转向有序，仿佛秩序是人类生存的必需品。② 对他来说，遗忘或忽略那些困扰我们生存的混乱并不能带来秩序；秩序是一种必要的发展，是一种可能带来希腊理想中精神升华的进步。③《葬礼进行曲》没有成为《英雄交响曲》的最后乐章，而是第二乐章，这并非偶然，因为这样痛苦就不会成为最后的结局。④我们可以这样解读贝多芬的诸多作品：苦难是不可避免的，但是与苦难抗争的勇气使生活有了意义。
questions.answer: 贝多芬在演奏时习惯用极大的力度提高音量，然后突然转为轻柔的乐段，在他之前很少有作曲家使用这种方式。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“Beethoven’s habit of increasing the volume with an extreme intensity ”为本句主干，其中，介词短语“of increasing the volume”作后置定语，修饰habit，此处 将名词habit转为动词即“习惯于/用”，此外with an extreme intensity 作状语，翻译需要前置。“and then abruptly following it with a sudden soft passage ”这部分是and连接的并列的动名词短语作介词of的宾语。此处注意passage本义是“章节、段落”，但鉴于上下文都在描述音乐，此处就译为“乐段”，“was only rarely used by composers before him. ”为整个句子的谓语部分，采用了被动句，翻译时将被动换为主动更符合汉语表达，即在他之前很少有作曲家使用这种方式。

questions.answer: 更为重要的是他的自由观，在他看来，自由与个人的权利和责任息息相关：他倡导思想自由和个人言论自由。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

"本句主干“Especially significant was his view of freedom”，采用了完全倒装结构，但此语序正好符合汉语表达习惯，可直接顺译为更为重要的是他的自由观。“which, for him, was associated with the rights and responsibilities of the individual:”为which引导的非限定性定语从句，先行词是freedom，译为“自由与...息息相关”，介词短语of personal expression作后置定语，修饰the rights and responsibilities ，译为个人的权利和责任。“of thought and of personal expression. ”均作后置定语，翻译时前置，即他倡导思想自由和个人言论自由。"

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

本句主干“One could interpret much of the work of Beethoven”one表示泛指可译为“人们，我们”这里work是“作品”而非“工作”的意思，此处译为人们会这样解读贝多芬的多数作品，“by saying that suffering is inevitable,”为介词短语作方式状语，修饰前面的One could interpret ...,其中“that suffering is inevitable,”作saying的宾语，这句译为苦难是不可避免的，“but the courage to fight it renders life worth living.”中the courage to fight it整体作这个分句的主语，其中动词不定式短语to fight it作后置定语修饰the coura，整体译为“与苦难抗争的勇气”。

sections.passage:
1 As many people hit middle age, they often start to notice that their memory and mental clarity are not what they used to be. 2 We suddenly can’t remember 1 we put the keys just a moment ago, or an old acquaintance ’s name, or the name of an old band we used to love.? 3 As the brain 2, we refer to these occurrences as “ senior moments. “? 4 3 seemingly innocent, this loss of mental focus can potentially have a(n) 4 impact on our professional, social, and personal 5.?
1 Neuroscientists, experts who study the nervous system, are increasingly showing that there ’s actually a lot that can be done. 2 It 6 out that the brain needs exercise in much the same way our muscles do, and the right mental 7 can significantly improve our basic cognitive 8.? 3 Thinking is essentially a 9 of making connections in the brain.? 4 To a certain extent, our ability to 10 in making the connections that drive intelligence is inherited.? 5 11, because these connections are made through effort and practice, scientists believe that intelligence can expand and fluctuate 12 mental effort.?
1 Now, a new Web-based company has taken it a step 13 and developed the first “ brain training program “ designed to actually help people improve and regain their mental 14.?
1 The Web-based program 15 you to systematically improve your memory and attention skills.? 2 The program keeps 16 of your progress and provides detailed feedback 17 your performance and improvement.? 3 Most importantly, it 18 modifies and enhances the games you play to 19 on the strengths you are developing — much like a(n) 20 exercise routine requires you to increase resistance and vary your muscle use.?

questions.explanation:
【答案解析】

空格所在句以举例论证的手法证明了观点，且出现了or...，or...表示并列关系的词，该句可解读如下：we put the keys...=an old acquaintance’s name=the name of an old band...，空格所在短语应与等式两边一样，都要表达记忆力的衰退，因此空格所在短语应表达“钥匙放在了何处”这一意思，故A选项where为正确答案。而B选项when（在时候）、C选项that（从句标志词）以及D选项why（为什么）均无法表示此意，予以排除。

【答案解析】

逻辑关系和词义辨析题。根据上文可知：人到中年记忆力大不如前，会突然记不起许多事情。因此该空格处应选择表示消极概念的词汇。纵观四个选项，A选项improves（改善）和C选项recovers（恢复）表达积极概念，因此首先予以排除。B选项fades（衰退）和D选项collapses（崩溃）表达消极概念，而后者多指人情绪失控，用在此处搭配不当，因此B选项为正确答案。

【答案解析】

经分析发现，空格所在句关系如下：seemingly innocent ≠this loss of mental focus can potentially have a (n) impact。前者说“看似无辜”，后者说“可能有影响”，由此可以判断，前后形成转折关系，而非条件关系，因此正确答案为D选项While（虽然，然而），而非A选项If（如果）。B选项Unless意为“除非，如果不”，C选项Once意为“一旦”，两者都是引导条件状语从句的逻辑连接词，不符合此处的逻辑关系，故均予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格所在句要表达的是：这种注意力的缺失有可能对……产生影响。上文提到人到中年后，会记不起许多事情。据此判断，注意力的缺失会给人们带来负面的影响。C选项damaging（有破坏性的，损害的）符合文意，因此为正确答案。而将A选项uneven（不公平的，不均匀的）、B选项limited（有限的）和D选项obscure（模糊的，不清楚的）代入原文，均不符合文意，故排除。

【答案解析】

空格前的and连接了professional,social以及personal三个形容词，所以空格处所填入的名词需要能同时被这三者修饰，且最切题。B选项environment（环境）不能被personal 修饰，首先予以排除。同时，第5题应该选一个与前文“当许多人步入中年时，他们往往开始发现自己的记忆力和思维清晰度不如以前了”的顺承概念，也就是表达出幸福现状的衰退，而不是前景的衰退。因此A选项wellbeing（幸福）最符合题意，为正确答案。而C选项relationship（关系）可与空格前的形容词搭配，所构成的短语personal relationship（人际关系）与social relationship（社会关系，人际关系）表意重复，故为干扰选项；D选项outlook （展望）不能表达对个人产生的影响，因此予以排除。

【答案解析】

固定搭配题。本题四个选项均可与out搭配，这就要求考生结合文意进行判断。空格前为It，而空格后有一个that引导的从句，即“大脑需……锻炼，……。”将A选项turns代入文中，turns out为固定搭配，意为“结果是，事实证明”，符合文意，故A选项为正确答案。B、C、D 三个选项均可与out进行搭配：finds out意为“发现，查明”，points out意为“指出”，figures out意为“计算出”，但代入文中，It指代不明，这三个选项均不符合原文意思。故排除。

【答案解析】

and之前的分句表示大脑需要锻炼，and之后的分句则说明这种适当的思维锻炼对人所产生的影响。C选项workouts正是“锻炼，训练”的意思，与前文的exercise呼应，为正确答案。而A选项roundabouts（绕道），B选项responses（反应）以及D选项associations（联想）与题意不符，均予以排除。

【答案解析】

第8题可顺势做出。空格与其前的cognitive（认知的）一起作improve的宾语，说明脑部训练改善了什么。四个选项中，只有认知功能是与记忆力有关的概念，因此B选项functions为正确答案。而A选项genre（体裁），C选项circumstances（环境）以及D选项criterion（标准，准则）与原文毫无关系，均予以排除

【答案解析】

空格所在句为主系表结构，系动词is前后表示并列关系，解读如下：Thinking=aof making connections in the brain，本空实际上是给thinking下一个定义，四个选项中与出inking一致性保持的最好的选项将会是正确答案。而思考是一个过程，这本身就是最合理的，因此D选项process（过程）为正确答案。而A选项channel（渠道）、B选项condition（条件）以及C选项sequence（顺序）均不符合文意，故不正确。

【答案解析】

词义辨析题。本题主要考查介词in的词组搭配。四个选项中的动词均可以与介词in搭配，这就要求考生必须在理解句意的基础上解题。空格所在句的主干部分是…ability…is inherited（……能力是与生俱来的）。本句中的动词不定式短语to in making the connections作后置定语，修饰主语ability ，本填空所在句的意思为：我们建立能够促进智能发展的链接的能力是与生俱来的。把C选项excel代入文中，可构成词组excel in，意为“善于”，句意通顺，故c选项为正确答案。将A选项persist (in)（坚持）；B选项believe (in)（信任）；D选项feature (in) （起重要作用）这三个选项代入原句，不符合文意，故均予以排除。

【答案解析】

空格前一句说道，我们善于建立能够促进智能发展的链接的能力是与生俱来的，而空格后一句却指出这些链接需要通过努力和练习来构建，前后两句是转折关系，故而D选项However（然而）正确。A选项Therefore表示因果关系；B选项Moreover表示递进关系，这两个选项与原文的逻辑关系不符，故不正确；C选项Otherwise虽然表示转折关系，但用于此处语义不通，故予以排除。

【答案解析】

逻辑关系题。空格后的mental effort与之前的these connections are made through effort and practice构成同义复现，因此mental effort对于推动智力发展是必不可少的。空格所在句可以理解为：由于这些链接需要通过努力和练习来构建，因此科学家相信智力的拓展和波动脑力活动。故A选项according to（取决于）符合文意。纵观四个选项，B选项regardless of（不管，不顾），c选项apart from（除了），D选项instead of（代替，而不是），这三个选项均与原文意思相反，属于反向干扰，故都不正确。

【答案解析】

空格所在句中的and后既然提到developed the first（初创），那这个公司自然是领先他人一步，能表示“进一步”的只有B选项further，故为正确答案。而A选项back（向后），C选项aside（在一边）以及D选项around（到处）与题意不符，均予以排除。

【答案解析】

文章第一段第➊句说到他们的记忆力和思维清晰度大不如前，而本段中提到这款“大脑训练程序”旨在帮助人们改善和恢复他们大脑的，可见此处的mental 与第一段第➊句中的mental clarity（思维清晰度）为同义呼应，而A选项sharpness（清晰度）与clarity恰为同义词，故A选项为正确答案。B选项stability的意思是“稳定性”，C选项framework的意思是“结构”，而D选项flexibility 的意思是“灵活性”，均不能与上文的clarity（清晰度）构成同义呼应，故不符合题意。

【答案解析】

空格所在句表达的是：这个基于网络的程序可以你系统地提高记忆力和注意力方面的技能。空格处所填的动词应强调的是这款程序所产生的效果，即系统地提高记忆力和注意力方面的技能。而D选项allows构成的短语allows sb. to do sth.的意思是“允许某人做某事”，代入文中，符合文意，因此为正确答案。A选项forces可构成词组forces sb. to do sth，意为“强迫某人做某事”，本文在介绍“大脑训练程序”时，感情色彩是中性的，而A选项的动作显然过于负面，不符合原文的感情色彩，故排除。B选项reminds可构成词组reminds sb. to do sth，表示“提醒某人做某事”，C选项hurries构成词组hurries sb. to do sth，意思是“催促某人做某事”��将这两个选项代入原文，不能表达产生效果的含义，因此都不符合原文语义。

【答案解析】

逻辑关系和词义辨析题。空格所在处表达的是：这个程序你的训练进度。B选项track代入文中，构成的短语keeps track of的意思是“跟踪，记录”，符合语义，因此B选项track 为正确答案。A选项hold可构成短语keeps hold of，意思是“紧握，抓住”，C选项order可构成短语keeps order of，意为“维持，维护”，代入原文，语义不通，故排除。而D选项pace需与介词with相搭配，构成的短语keeps pace with表示“跟上，保持同步”，而此处的介词为of，因此也不正确。

【答案解析】

固定搭配题。空格所在处表达的是：你的表现和进步情况提供详细的反馈。而短语feedback on的意思是“对...的反馈”，因此选择D选项on。虽然feedback不能与其余三个选项构成搭配，但此空前的动词provides可与其构成相关短语provide sth. to/for sb.和provide sb. with sth. （为某人提供某物），因此A、B、C三个选项具有一定的干扰性。 而本句中，空格处所填的介词并非与动词provides相搭配。故排除这三个选项。

【答案解析】

词义辨析题。根据上下文语境，可以判断本句是在描述这一程序的功能及作用，根据句���，空格处应填入表示频率的副词。该空格所在部分表达的是：这一程序会调整和升级你所玩的游戏。纵观四个选项，结合句意判断，C选项constantly（不断地）为符合文意的答案。A选项irregularly（不规则地），不符合句意，故排除。B选项habitually（习惯地），一般用来说明人的动作，不适用于此处。D选项unusually（异乎寻常地），代入原文，逻辑不通，故不正确。

【答案解析】

本题考查动词与on的搭配。本词组处于一个表目的的不定式中，它是此前it constantly modifies and enhances the games you play的目的。词组的宾语是the strengths you are developing，而由you are developing这一现在进行时可知strengths本身是在不断发展中的，而constantly modifies and enhances也表示持续地调整和提升，由复现原则，C选项build与on搭配可表达一种持续地增强的概念，与developing和modifies and enhances具有明显的一致性，因此C选项为正确答案。A选项carry可构成carry on，意思是“继续进行（尤指迎着困难）”，不符合文意。B选项put代入文中，构成短语put on，意思是“穿上，上演”，不能与strengths搭配，故而排除。D选项take与on搭配，构成短语take on，意思是“呈现（面貌等）；承担（责任等）”，与原文语义不符，因此也不正确。

【答案解析】

表示并列关系的like连接的前后两个分句可解读如下：it…build on the strengths...=a（an）exercise routine…从感情色彩来讲，既然这种程序可以使我们变得更强，那么第20空就应该填入一个褒义词。B选项effective（有效的）符合文章的感情色彩，故B选项正确。A选项risky（冒险的）、C选项idle（闲置的）以及D选项familiar（熟悉的）均属于中性词汇，予以排除。

sections.passage:
1 【A】 Some archaeological sites have always been easily observable — for example, the Parthenon in Athens, Greece; the pyramids of Giza in Egypt; and the megaliths of Stonehenge in southern England. 2 But these sites are exceptions to the norm. 3 Most archaeological sites have been located by means of careful searching, while many others have been discovered by accident. 4 Olduvai Gorge, an early hominid site in Tanzania, was found by a butterfly hunter who literally fell into its deep valley in 1911. 5 Thousands of Aztec artifacts came to light during the digging of the Mexico City subway in the 1970s.
1 【B】 In another case, American archaeologists René million and George Cowgill spent years systematically mapping the entire city of Teotihuacan in the valley of Mexico near what is now Mexico City. 2 At its peak around AD600, this city was one of the largest human settlements in the world. 3 The researchers mapped not only the city’s vast and ornate ceremonial areas, but also hundreds of simpler apartment complexes where common people lived.
1 【C】 How do archaeologists know where to find what they are looking for when there is nothing visible on the surface of the ground? 2 Typically, they survey and sample (make test excavations on) large areas of terrain to determine where excavation will yield useful information. 3 Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.
1 【D】 Surveys can cover a single large settlement or entire landscapes. 2 In one case, many researchers working around the ancient Maya city of Copán, Honduras, have located hundreds of small rural villages and individual dwellings by using aerial photographs and by making surveys on foot. 3 The resulting settlement maps show how the distribution and density of the rural population around the city changed dramatically between AD500 and 850, when Copán collapsed.
1 【E】 To find their sites, archaeologists today rely heavily on systematic survey methods and a variety of high-technology tools and techniques. 2 Airborne technologies, such as different types of radar and photographic equipment carried by airplanes or spacecraft, allow archaeologists to learn about what lies beneath the ground without digging. 3 Aerial surveys locate general areas of interest or larger buried features, such as ancient buildings or fields.
1 【F】 Most archaeological sites, however, are discovered by archaeologists who have set out to look for them. 2 Such searches can take years. 3 British archaeologist Howard Carter knew that the tomb of the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamen existed from information found in other sites. 4 Carter sifted through rubble in the Valley of the King for seven years before he located the tomb in 1922. 5 In the late 1800s British archaeologist Sir Arthur Eyan combed antique dealers ’ stores in Athens, Greece. 6 He was searching for tiny engraved seals attributed to the ancient Mycenaean culture that dominated Greece from the 1400s to 1200sBC. 7 Evas ’s interpretations of those engravings eventually led them to find the Minoan palace at Knossos (knosós) on the island of Crete, in 1900.
1 【G】 Ground surveys allow archaeologists to pinpoint the places where digs will be successful 2 Most ground surveys involve a lot of walking, looking for surface clues such as small fragments of pottery 3 They often include a certain amounts of digging to test for buried materials at selected points across a landscape. 4 Archaeologists also may locate buried remains by using such technologies as ground radar, magnetic-field recording, and metal detector. 5 Archaeologists commonly use computers to map sites and the landscapes around sites. 6 Two and three-dimensional maps are helpful tools in planning excavations, illustrating how sites look, and presenting the results of archaeological research.
1 41.? 2 —>【A】 3 —>42.? 4 —>【E】 5 —>43.? 6 —>44.? 7 —>45.?

questions.explanation:
【考点分析】

首段特点及作用


【选项分析】

文首段通常用于引入主题或交代与主题相关的背景，内容相对独立，不应存在与上文相衔接的内容,也不应存在文意缺漏现象。纵观各段，[A]、[E]段已确定位置，[B]段段首In another case和[F]段首句however均体现与上文衔接关系，不能作为首段; 而[D]段首句Surveys一词指代不明,作为首段过于突兀。

 

【答案解析】

由上文分析可知[C][G]段为备选项。

若[C]段为首段，可与[A]段构成设问引题——铺垫背景”的逻辑顺序: [C]段设问引题“考古学家遗址搜寻办法”，并暗示指出“有迹可循条件下可肉眼观测，无迹可寻条件下则通过勘测及抽样(即试掘)方式” ，[A]随后铺陈背景，明晰三种遗址发现方式(一、地表有迹可循，二、仔细搜寻，三、偶然发现)，其中第一种完全对应[C]段nothing visible on the surface of the ground暗藏之意。另外,设问也是常用的开篇方法。

若[G]段为首段，那么与[A]段构成“地面勘测及其高科技手段一>考古遗址三种发现途径”衔接。而仔细研读会发现，[G]段ground surveys应该涵盖在[A]段第二种方式“仔细搜查”当中,故排除。

【考点分析】

上下文衔接


【选项分析】

本段位于已定位的[A]、[E]段之间，故应从这两个已知段落入手。[A]段介绍的三种途径中,第一、三种都以事例加以说明，而占比很大的第二种却并未被佐证。暗示下文将具体介绍“考古学家如何费时费力仔细搜寻发现遗址”；E段介绍现在考古用到的方法和手段，提示上文可能涉及以前考古用到的方法和手段。纵观剩余段落([F]、[B]、[D]、[G]段)，[F]段所示事例及考古方法手段更为贴近。


【答案分析】

由上文分析可知[F]段可能与[A]段衔接。

[F]段指出“大多数遗址需要考古学家花费数年专门仔细搜寻才最终被发现”，与[A7段所述两种考古捷径正好形成转折关系，F段首句however所示段际逻辑关系成立。同时F段列举的例子中，过去的考古学家只能通过仔细考察碎石瓦砾、排查古董商店等传统方法来寻找遗址的蛛丝马迹，与E段“现在考古学家主要依靠系统的勘测方法和高科技手段搜寻遗址”在时间上、内容上都衔接紧密,合乎逻辑。

【考点分析】

上下文衔接


【选项分析】

根据已定位的[E]段内容“当代考古高科技手段,并列举空中勘测技术手段及可定位大致目标区域”可知,本段可能探及���为精准的定位手段。纵观剩余段落(B、D、G段)，G段所示“地面勘测可准确定位有效挖掘位置”更为贴合。


【答案分析】

由上文分析可知[G]段可能与[E]段衔接。

[G]段首Ground surveys与[E]段末句Aerial surveys相对,分别介绍“用于大致定位考古遗址的空中勘测”和“用于准确定位考古遗址的地面勘测”，两者衔接符合考古勘测的一般步骤"先粗略后精准”，照应[E]段首句中systematic survey(系统性勘测); 另外，两段均涉及两种勘测方法所用到的高科技技术,也与E段首句中a variety of high-technology tools and techniques相照应,两段构成“总一分”结构。

【考点分析】

上下文衔接和逻辑衔接词


【选项分析】

在前文[E]、[G]两段已经准确定位考古遗址的基础上,下文很可能涉及在考古遗址上的具体勘测工作。


【答案分析】

[B]、[D]可能与上文衔接。

剩余两个备选项[B]、[D]由逻辑衔接词In another case In one case即可确定顺序为[D]→[B]。从内容上看，[D]段首句总述“勘测可以覆盖某一居住点也可以覆盖整个区域”其后以In one case引出例证“测覆盖某一居住地(a single large settlement)”，[B]段以In another case引出例证“勘测覆盖整个区域(entire landscapes)”，两段构成“总一分”结构。另外上文E、G两段侧重介绍“考古遗址的定位”，[D]、[B]两段侧重介绍“考古勘测的范围”，两者衔接符合“先定位,后勘测”的做事步骤, 故[D]、[B]与前文衔接顺畅。


至此,全文的顺序确定为[C]→[A]→[F]→[E]→[G]→[D]→[B]。在上述排序的基础之上,再通读一遍检查思路是否清晰连贯，结构是否完整，段间层次关系是否恰当。在整体审视之后,方可最终确定��

【选项分析】

在前文[E]、[G]两段已经准确定位考古遗址的基础上,下文很可能涉及在考古遗址上的具体勘测工作。


【答案分析】

[B]、[D]可能与上文衔接。

剩余两个备选项[B]、[D]由逻辑衔接词In another case In one case即可确定顺序为[D]→[B]。从内容上看，[D]段首句总述“勘测可以覆盖某一居住点也可以覆盖整个区域”其后以In one case引出例证“测覆盖某一居住地(a single large settlement)”，[B]段以In another case引出例证“勘测覆盖整个区域(entire landscapes)”，两段构成“总一分”结构。另外上文E、G两段侧重介绍“考古遗址的定位”，[D]、[B]两段侧重介绍“考古勘测的范围”，两者衔接符合“先定位,后勘测”的做事步骤, 故[D]、[B]与前文衔接顺畅。


至此,全文的顺序确定为[C]→[A]→[F]→[E]→[G]→[D]→[B]。在上述排序的基础之上,再通读一遍检查思路是否清晰连贯，结构是否完整，段间层次关系是否恰当。在整体审视之后,方可最终确定。

sections.passage:
1 In order to " change lives for the better " and reduce " dependency", George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, introduced the " upfront work search " scheme. 2 Only if the jobless arrive at the jobcentre with a CV, register for online job search, and start looking for work will they be eligible for benefit —— and then they should report weekly rather than fortnightly.? 3 What could be more reasonable?
1 More apparent reasonableness followed. 2 There will now be a seven-day wait for the jobseeker ’s allowance. 3 " Those first few days should be spent looking for work, not looking to sign on. " he claimed.? 4 " We ’re doing these things because we know they help people stay off benefits and help those on benefits get into work faster." 5 Help? 6 Really? 7 On first hearing, this was the socially concerned chancellor, trying to change lives for the better, complete with "reforms" to an obviously indulgent system that demands too little effort from the newly unemployed to find work, and subsidises laziness. 8 What motivated him, we were to understand, was his zeal for "fundamental fairness"— protecting the taxpayer, controlling spending and ensuring that only the most deserving claimants received their benefits.?
1 Losing a job is hurting: you don 't skip down to the jobcentre with a song in your heart, delighted at the prospect of doubling your income from the generous state.? 2 It is financially terrifying, psychologically embarrassing and you know that support is minimal and extraordinarily hard to get. 3 You are now not wanted; you are now excluded from the work environment that offers purpose and structure in your life. 4 Worse, the crucial income to feed yourself and your family and pay the bills has disappeared. 5 Ask anyone newly unemployed what they want and the answer is always: a job.
1 But in Osborneland, your first instinct is to fall into dependency — permanent dependency if you can get it — supported by a state only too ready to indulge your falsehood. 2 It is as though 20 years of ever-tougher reforms of the job search and benefit administration system never happened. 3 The principle of British welfare is no longer that you can insure yourself against the risk of unemployment and receive unconditional payments if the disaster happens. 4 Even the very phrase "jobseeker 's allowance" is about redefining the unemployed as a " jobseeker " who had no fundamental right to a benefit he or she has earned through making national insurance contributions. 5 Instead, the claimant receives a time-limited " allowance," conditional on actively seeking a job; no entitlement and no insurance, at £71.70 a week, one of the least generous in the EU.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

George Osborne’ scheme was intended to______ .

乔治·奥斯本计划旨在______ 。

A. provide the unemployed with easier access to benefits

   给失业者提供更便利的获得救济的途径

B. encourage jobseekers’ active engagement in job seeking

   鼓励求职者积极地寻找工作

C. motivate the unemployed to report voluntarily

   激励失业者自愿报到

D. guarantee jobseekers’ legitimate right to benefits

   保证求职者获得救济的合法权利


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的George Osborne和scheme，可迅速定位到1段1句。该句可知，奧斯本这一计划的目的是“让生活变得更美好”，并减少“依赖性”。紧接着2句指出：失业者只有带上简历到就业中心报到，在网上注册求职，并开始找工作，才有资格获得失业救济金。由此可知，奥斯本这一计划的目的是鼓励失业者积极寻找工作，以此减少他们的“依赖性”。B选项是对原文文意的合理概括，因此正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 给失业者提供更便利的获得救济的途径：利用1段2句中的benefit设置干扰。A选项与1段2句所传达出的“失业者获得救济的条件变得更严苛”这一信息相悖，故排除。

【偷换功概念】C 激励失业者自愿报到：选项利用1段2句中的“they should report...”设置干扰，这是奥斯本计划的具体要求，并非其意图，故排除。

【无中生有】D 保证求职者获得救济的合法权利：利用1段2句中的benefit设置干扰，而1段1句破折号后的内容（...rather than fortnightly）暗示，求职者此前即可获得救济，故D选项中的guarantee（保证）无从体现，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The phrase “ to sign on”（Line3，Para.2）most probably means ______ .

2段2行的短语to sign on最可能意为______。

A. to check on the availability of jobs at the jobcentre

   查看就业中心有无工作机会

B. to accept the government’s restrictions on the allowance

   接受政府对津贴的限制

C. to register for an allowance from the government

   登记申领政府津贴

D. to attend a governmental job-training program

   参加政府的职业培训项目


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息可定位到2段3句。根据该句后半句not looking to sign on中的not可知，短语looking to sign on的意思与前半句中looking for work的意思恰好相反。结合上下文，2句提到“求职者将要经过一个七天的等待期才能拿到失业津贴”，4句指出“这样做的目的是帮助那些依靠救济的人更快地找到工作”，可以进一步推断to sign on即“申领政府津贴”。因此，C选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 查看就业中心有无工作机会：选项中的“查看就业中心有无工作机会”与原文中的looking for work同义，因此A选项属于反向干扰，故排除。

【答非所问】B 接受政府对津贴的限制：选项利用4段5句中的a time-limited “allowance”设置干扰，其与to sign on所在的语境无关，故排除。

【无中生有】D 参加政府的职业培训项目：选项中的a governmental job-training program在原文并未被提及，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

What prompted the chancellor to develop his scheme？

促使财相生成其计划的动因是什么?

A. A desire to secure a better life for all.

   确保所有人拥有更好生活的愿望

B. An eagerness to protect the unemployed.

   保护失业者的渴望

C. An urge to be generous to the claimants.

   对申请人表示慷慨的强烈愿望

D. A passion to ensure fairness for taxpayers.

   确保纳税者公平的���情


【定位及答案】

题干中的What prompted the chancellor与2段8句中的What motivated him表意相同，故可定位至2段8句。该句指出“他会怎么做（开展计划）的动力是他对‘基本公平’的热情——保护纳税人，……”，D选项是对原文中his zeal for“fundamental fairness”-protecting the taxpayer的同义转述，故为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【答非所问】A 确保所有人拥有更好生活的愿望：选项利用2段7句中的trying to change lives for the better设置干扰，但这是“乍听之下”的解释，并不是奥斯本的真正动机，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 保护失业者的渴望：选项将2段8句“...protecting the taxpayer...”中的the taxpayer偷换成了the unemployed，故排除。

【反向干扰】C 对申请人表示慷慨的强烈愿望：由2段8句中的“确保只有最需要救济的申请人才能领到补贴”可知，奥斯本对申请人更加“小气”，而非“慷慨”，故排除。

【题目及选项概览】

According to Paragraph 3, being unemployed makes one feel ______ .

根据第三段可知,失业会使人们感到______ 。

A.uneasy   不安

B.enraged    愤怒

C.insulted    羞辱

D.guilty    内疚


【定位及答案】

题干已经定位于第3段。题干中的being unemployed（失业）相当于第三段首句的Losing a job，此句提到，失去工作令人感到痛苦（hurting）。紧接着第2句话进一步描述了失业者的痛苦，即“失业是经济上的劫难、心理上的尴尬”，而A选项uneasy（不安的）恰好体现了失业者的感受，因此A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【过度推理】B选项enraged意为“愤怒的”，C选项insulted意为“羞辱的”，这两项表达的情感太过激烈，不能反映失业者的真实感受，属于过度推理，故排除。

【无中生有】D guilty（内疚的）：在原文没有任何依据，属于无中生有。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

To which of the following would the author most probably agree？

作者最有可能同意下列哪项说法?

A. The British welfare system indulges jobseekers’ laziness.

   英国福利体制助长求职者的惰性

B. Osborne's reforms will reduce the risk of unemployment.

   奥斯本的改革会降低失业的风险

C. The jobseekers’ allowance has met their actual needs.

   求职者的津贴满足了他们的实际需要

D. Unemployment benefits should not be made conditional.

   失业救济金不应该有附加条件


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者的观点态度，根据顺序命题原则，可定位至文章第4段。该段中，作者对奥斯本的“预备求职”计划进行了评判：20年来，英国求职和福利管理体制经过了日益严厉的改革，其早已不能让失业者获得无条件的救济，以抵御灾难；而奥斯本的“预备求职”计划所提供的“失业津贴”也是有时间限制的，且必须符合“积极寻找工作”这一条件，作者认为“这是欧盟国家中最不慷慨的津贴之一”。言下之意，作者对该“津贴”持批判态度，即他认为“失业救济金不能有时间和其他条件限制”。综上所述，D选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】由上述分析可进一步得知：英国福利体制并不会助长求职者的惰性；求职者的津贴也不能满足其实际需要。因此，排除A、C。

【偷换概念】B 奥斯本的改革会降低失业的风险：选项利用4段3句中的the risk of unemployment设置干扰，该句指出“英国社会福利的原则不再是……保证自己可以抵御失业的风险”，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text2
sections.passage:
1 All around the world, lawyers generate more hostility than the members of any other profession — with the possible exception of journalism. 2 But there are few places where clients have more grounds for complaint than America.
1 During the decade before the economic crisis, spending on legal services in America grew twice as fast as inflation. 2 The best lawyers made skyscrapers-full of money, tempting ever more students to pile into law schools. 3 But most law graduates never get a big-firm job. 4 Many of them instead become the kind of nuisance-lawsuit filer that makes the tort system a costly nightmare.?
1 There are many reasons for this. 2 One is the excessive costs of a legal education. 3 There is just one path for a lawyer in most American states: a four-year undergraduate degree in some unrelated subject, then a three-year law degree at one of 200 law schools authorized by the American Bar Association and an expensive preparation for the bar exam. 4 This leaves today ’s average law-school graduate with $100,000 of debt on top of undergraduate debts.? 5 Law-school debt means that they have to work fearsomely hard.
1 Reforming the system would help both lawyers and their customers. 2 Sensible ideas have been around for a long time, but the state-level bodies that govern the profession have been too conservative to implement them. 3 One idea is to allow people to study law as an undergraduate degree. 4 Another is to let students sit for the bar after only two years of law school. 5 If the bar exam is truly a stern enough test for a would-be lawyer, those who can sit it earlier should be allowed to do so.? 6 Students who do not need the extra training could cut their debt mountain by a third.
1 The other reason why costs are so high is the restrictive guild-like ownership structure of the business. 2 Except in the District of Columbia, non-lawyers may not own any share of a law firm. 
 3 This keeps fees high and innovation slow. 4 There is pressure for change from within the profession, but opponents of change among the regulators insist that keeping outsiders out of a law firm isolates lawyers from the pressure to make money rather than serve clients ethically.?
1 In fact, allowing non-lawyers to own shares in law firms would reduce costs and improve services to customers, by encouraging law firms to use technology and to employ professional managers to focus on improving firms’ efficiency. 2 After all, other countries, such as Australia and Britain, have started liberalizing their legal professions. 3 America should follow.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

A lot of students take up law as their profession due to ______ .

许多学生从事法律行业是因为______ 。

A. the growing demand from clients

    委托人日益增长的诉讼需求

B. the increasing pressure of inflation

    不断增加的通货膨胀压力

C. the prospect of working in big firms

    在大公司工作的前景

D. the attraction of financial rewards

    经济回报的吸引力


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的students和law可迅速定位到2段2句，该句提到：那些最好的律师挣的钱能够填满整幢摩天大楼，这吸引着越来越多的学生挤进法学院。由此可知，正是律师的高收入吸引很多学生以律师为职业。D选项与此表述相符，故为正确答案。其中，D选项中的attraction（吸引）对应2段2句的tempting（吸引），financial rewards（经济回报）对应skyscrapers-full of money（巨额财富）。


【错选分析】

【词汇干扰】A 委托人日益增长的诉讼需求：选项利用1段2句中的clients设置干扰，该句指出“美国的委托人有更多理由抱怨”，并非说明其有日益增长的诉讼需求，故排除。

【词汇干扰】B 不断增加的通货膨胀压力：选项利用2段1句中的inflation设置干扰，该句指出“美国人花费在法律服务上的费用增长速度为通货膨胀增长速度的两倍”，其意在说明“法律服务费用增长速度很快”，并未谈论通货膨胀与学生选择律师职业的关系，故排除。

【偷换概念】C 在大公司工作的前景：利用2段3句中的get a big-firm job设置干扰，该句提及“很多法学毕业生从未得到在大公司工作的机会”，显然“在大公司工作的前景”不是学生选择律师职业的诱因，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following adds to the costs of legal education in most American states？

下面哪项增加了在美国大多数州接受法律教育的费用?

A. Higher tuition fees for undergraduate studies.

    较高的本科学费

B. Admissions approval from the bar association.

    律师协会的入学许可

C. Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in another major.

    攻读另一专业的学士学位

D. Receiving training by professional associations.

    接受专业协会的培训


【定位及答案】

根据题干信息可定位到3段2、3句，2句指出法学教育费用过高，3句解释了法学教育费用过高的原因：四年与法学不相关的本科学习，三年的法学学位学习，并需要准备一个昂贵的律师资格考试。由此可见，题干所说的增加了法学教育成本的应该是四年与法学不相关的本科学习，故C选项为正确答案。其中，C选项中Pursuing a bachelor’s degree（攻读学士学位）同义替换了原文中的a four-year undergraduate degree，in another major（另一专业）是对in some unrelated subject的同义替换。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 较高的本科学费：利用3段4句设置干扰，原文的确提及“法学院毕业生背负本科阶段债务”，但并未明确说明“其因本科学费较高而负债”，故排除。

【偷换概念】B 律师协会的入学许可：利用3段3句中的authorized by the American Bar Association设置干扰，该句意为“学生必须在美国律师协会授权的法学院中进行法学学位学习”，并非“学生进入法学院学习需得到律师协会的许可”，故排除B选项。

【词汇干扰】D 接受专业协会的培训：选项利用4段6句中的training设置干扰，此处的training指的是在法学院第三年的学习，而非专业协会的培训，因此予以排除。

choices.label: B
choices.text: the rigid bodies governing the profession

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Hindrance to the reform of the legal system originates from ______ .

法律制度改革的障碍源于______。

A. lawyers’ and clients’ strong resistance

    律师和委托人的强烈反对

B. the rigid bodies governing the profession

    行业监管机构的死板

C. the stern exam for would-be lawyers

    严格的准律师资格考试

D. non-professionals’ sharp criticism

    非专业人士的尖锐批评


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的the reform of the legal system可迅速定位到4段1句。该句提出改革的好处，即体制改革对律师和客户双方都有利。而2句中的逻辑关联词but提示句意出现了转折，它后面的句子指出了改革的阻力，即管理该行业的州级政府机关一直过于保守，而没能实施这些建议。B选项中的bodies governing the profession相当于原文4段2句的bodies that govern the profession，rigid（僵硬的，死板的）与4段2句中conservative一词的意思相近，故B选项是原文的同义替换，为正确选项。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 律师和委托人的强烈反对：4段1句提到“改革这种体制将对律师和客户双方都有利”。自然，律师和客户都会支持法律体制的改革，故排除。

【细节干扰】C 严格的准律师资格考试：由4段4、5句可知，让法学院学生提前一年参加律师资格考试是法作体制改革的方法之一，律师资格考试并不属于改革阻力，故排除。

【无中生有】D 非专业人士的尖锐批评：选项无法在原文找到依据，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The guild-like ownership structure is considered “restrictive” partly because it______ .

类似公会的所有权结构被认为是“限制性的”，部分原因是______。

A. bans outsiders’ involvement in the profession

    禁止外人介入律师行业

B. keeps lawyers from holding law-firm shares

    阻止律师持法律事务所股份

C. aggravates the ethical situation in the trade

    恶化行业的职业道德

D. prevents lawyers from gaining due profits

    妨碍律师获取应得的报酬


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的guild-like ownership structure和restrictive，可定位到5段1句。该句提出，律师成本高的另一原因是这一行业限制性的协会式所有权体制。接下来，2句对其进行了解释说明。由2句可知，非律师人员不能拥有律师事务所的股份。也就是说，“限制性的”原因是禁止非律师人员介入律师行业，因此A选项正确。此外，4句谈到监管机构中的反对变革者坚持认为应该将局外人排除在律师事务所之外，进一步印证A选项是正确答案。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】B 阻止律师持法律事务所股份：由5段2句可知，协会式所有权体制限制非律师人员持法律事务所股份，而非限制律师，B选项将文中的non-lawyers偷换成lawyers，故排除。

【反向干扰】5段4句指出“将局外人排除在律师事务所之外能够确保律师在为客户服务时不是屈从于赚钱的压力，而是恪守职业道德”，由此可知，协会式所有权体制能够确保律师恪守职业道德，并获得应得的报酬。C、D两个选项与原文表意相悖，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

In this text, the author mainly discusses______ .

在本文中，作者主要讨论的是_____。

A. flawed ownership of America’s law firms and its causes

    美国律师事务所所有权存在的问题及其形成原因

B. the factors that help make a successful lawyer in America

    在美国成为一个成功律师的促成因素

C. a problem in America’s legal profession and solutions to it

    美国法律行业的问题及其解决方案

D. the role of undergraduate studies in America’s legal education

    本科学习在美国法学教育中的作用


【定位及答案】

本题是文章主旨题，考查考生对文章中心思想的理解。这篇短文是典型的“描述现象——提出问题——分析问题——解决问题”类议论文。文章首先通过叙述许多人对律师行业的不满，引出美国律师行业存在的问题：美国法律服务费用高昂。接着分析了造成此问题的两方面原因，即第3段说到的法学教育费用过高和第5段指出的体制问题，并分别在第4段和第6段提出了相应的解决办法：改革法学教育体制以及变革律师行业所有权体制。而四个选项中，C选项概括了这篇文章的主旨，故为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【以偏概全】A 美国律师事务所所有权存在的问题及其形成原因：选项为文章5段内容，不能综合概括全文主旨，故排除。

【无中生有】B 在美国成为一个成功律师的促成因素：文章中仅3段3句提到了“成为一名律师所必须接受的教育过程”，但并未提及“在美国成为一个成功律师的促成因素”，故排除。

【无中生有】D 本科学习在美国法学教育中的作用：3段3句提到“要成为一名律师须接受四年非法学专业的本科学习”，但并未提到“本科学习的作用”，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text3
sections.passage:
1 The US $ 3-million Fundamental Physics Prize is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year’s award in March. 2 And it is far from the only one of its type. 3 As a News Feature article in Nature discusses, a string of lucrative awards for researchers have joined the Nobel Prizes in recent years. 4 Many, like the Fundamental Physics Prize, are funded from the telephone-number-sized bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs. 5 These benefactors have succeeded in their chosen fields, they say, and they want to use their wealth to draw attention to those who have succeeded in science.?
1 What ’s not to like? 2 Quite a lot, according to a handful of scientists quoted in the News Feature. 3 You cannot buy class, as the old saying goes, and these upstart entrepreneurs cannot buy their prizes the prestige of the Nobels. 4 The new awards are an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them, say scientists. 5 They could distort the achievement-based system of peer-review-led research.? 6 They could cement the status quo of peer-reviewed research. 7 They do not fund peer-reviewed research. 8 They perpetuate the myth of the lone genius.
1 The goals of the prize-givers seem as scattered as the criticism. 2 Some want to shock, others to draw people into science, or to better reward those who have made their careers in research.
1 As Nature has pointed out before, there are some legitimate concerns about how science prizes — both new and old — are distributed. 2 The Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, launched this year, takes an unrepresentative view of what the life sciences include. 3 But the Nobel Foundation’s limit of three recipients per prize, each of whom must still be living, has long been outgrown by the collaborative nature of modern research — as will be demonstrated by the inevitable row over who is ignored when it comes to acknowledging the discovery of the Higgs boson.? 4 The Nobels were, of course, themselves set up by a very rich individual who had decided what he wanted to do with his own money. 5 Time, rather than intention, has given them legitimacy.?
1 As much as some scientists may complain about the new awards, two things seem clear. 2 First, most researchers would accept such a prize if they were offered one. 3 Second, it is surely a good thing that the money and attention come to science rather than go elsewhere. 4 It is fair to criticize and question the mechanism — that is the culture of research, after all — but it is the prize-givers ’ money to do with as they please. 5 It is wise to take such gifts with gratitude and grace.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The Fundamental Physics Prize is seen as______ .

基础物理学奖被视作______ 。

A. a symbol of the entrepreneurs’ wealth

    企业家财富的象征

B. a possible replacement of the Nobel Prizes

    诺贝尔奖的一个可能的替代品

C. an example of banks’ investments

    银行家投资的一个例子

D. a handsome reward for researchers

    对研究人员可观的奖励


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的专有名词Fundamental physics prize可迅速定位到1段1句。但该句只是蜻蜓点水地提到这一奖项，2句指出这一类型的奖项不止基础物理学奖一个。3句阐明还有一系列奖金和诺贝尔奖一样丰厚的科研奖项（lucrative awards for researchers），言下之意，“基础物理学奖”被看作奖金丰厚的科研奖项。D选项中的reward对应1段3句的awards，handsome（可观的）则对应原文中的lucrative（获利多的），for researchers属于原文再现，因此D选项是对原文的同义替换，为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 企业家财富的象征：由1段4句可知，基础物理学奖是由互联网企业家（Internet entrepreneurs）资助设立的，5句进一步指出这些资助者想用他们的财富（use their wealth）使大家关注已经在科学上获得成功的人，原文并未说明该奖项是他们财富的象征（symbol），故排除。

【细节干扰】B 诺贝尔奖的一个可能的替代品：利用1段3句中的the Nobel Prizes设置干扰，该句意在说明基础物理学奖的奖金与诺贝尔奖一样丰厚，并未暗示其可能替代诺贝尔奖，故排除。

【词汇干扰】C 银行家投资的一个例子：利用1段4句中的bank一词设置干扰，文中没有任何信息与“银行家投资”对应，故排除。

choices.label: B
choices.text: the founders of the new awards

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The critics think that the new awards will most benefit______ .

批评者认为,新奖项最大的获益者是______。

A. the profit-oriented scientists

    以利润为导向的科学家

B. the founders of the new awards

    新奖项的创建者

C. the achievement-based system

    基于成就的评价体系

D. peer-review-led research

    同行评议主导的研究


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的The critics可定位至2段，该段1句（What’s not to like？）和2句中的Quite a lot表明对于新奖项存在批评之声。4句指出批评者（科学家）的观点：这些新奖项的背后是其设立者们一种自抬身价的举动。言下之意，批评者认为设立者创建新奖项是由利益驱动，其最大受益者是奖项设立者本身。B选项是对原文的合理推断，故正确。


【错选分析】

【无中生有】A 以利润为导向的科学家：该选项的内容在原文中并未涉及，故排除。

【反向干扰】C、D两个选项均利用2段5句设置干扰，该句提出“它们（新奖项）会扭曲基于成就的、同行评议主导的研究体系”。由distort（扭曲）可知，这些新奖项对the achievement-based system和peer-review-led research都是不利的，因此排除C选项和D选项。

choices.label: B
choices.text: the joint effort of modern researchers

choices.label: C
choices.text: legitimate concerns over the new prizes

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The discovery of the Higgs boson is a typical case which involves______ .

希格斯玻色子的发现是一个涉及到______的典型案例。

A. controversies over the recipients' status

    有关获奖人身份的争议

B. the joint effort of modern researchers

    现代研究人员的共同努力

C. legitimate concerns over the new prizes

    对新奖项的合理关注

D. the demonstration of research findings

    研究成果的展示


【定位及答案】

由题干中的关键词The discovery of the Higgs boson定位位到4段3句。该句破折号后边提到了希格斯玻色子案例，其目的是为了证明破折号之前的内容，即诺贝尔奖的局限性（每个奖项只能有三名获奖人）被现代科学研究的协作本质所超越。换言之，现代科学研究是所有研究人员共同协作和努力的结果，这也正是希格斯玻色子案例典型的原因。因此B选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 有关获奖人身份的争议：4段3句指出，当提到奖励希格斯玻色子的发现时，就不可避免地会争论“谁被忽略了”这个问题。由此可知，原文提到的争论是“谁被忽略了”，而非有关获奖人身份的问题，A选项属于曲解文意，故不正确。

【答非所问】C 对新奖项的合理关注：选项利用4段1句中的legitimate concerns设置干扰，显然此句与希格斯玻色子无关，不是此典型案例直接涉及（involves）的内容，故排除。

【词汇干扰】D 研究成果的展示：选项中的demonstration一词是4段3句中demonstrated的同根词，但原文未提及research findings（研究成果）这一概念，因此该选项是利用原文词汇设置的干扰项，故不正确。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

According to Paragraph 4，which of the following is true of the Nobels？

第四段中有关诺贝尔奖的内容以下哪项正���?

A. Their endurance has done justice to them.

    长期持续使其价值得以充分发挥

B. Their legitimacy has long been in dispute.

    它们的合理性长期以来一直存在争议

C. They are the most representative honor.

    它们是最有代表性的荣誉

D. History has never cast doubt on them.

    历史从来没有对它们产生怀疑


【定位及答案】

根据题干可直接定位到第4段，该段5句指出：是时间，而不是意图，给予诺贝尔奖以合理性。即“诺贝尔奖延续至今使其合理地位得以确立，并确保其价值得到充分发挥，与设立者的初衷没有关系”。A选项与此表述相同，故正确。


【错选分析】

【词汇干扰】B 它们的合理性长期以来一直存在争议：4段5句只提及时间证明了诺贝尔奖的合理性，但并未指出它们的合理性长期以来一直存在争议，该选项是运用文章4段5句的legitimacy设置的干扰项，故排除。

【无中生有】C 它们是最有代表性的荣誉：选项在第四段中并未提及，故排除。

【反向干扰】D 历史从来没有对它们产生怀疑：选项中never一词太过绝对，且根据对4段3句的分析可知，诺贝尔奖是有局限性的，是受到过质疑的，因此D选项不正确。

choices.label: B
choices.text: harmful to the culture of research

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

The author believes that the new awards are______ .

作者认为新奖项______。

A. acceptable despite the criticism

    尽管受到批评但是可以接受

B. harmful to the culture of research

    对科研文化是有害的

C. subject to undesirable changes

    遭受不受欢迎的变化

D. unworthy of public attention

    不值得公众关注


【定位及答案】

题目涉及作者的态度，此类试题答案一般出自文末，结合关键词the new awards可定位到第5段。综合该段4句和5句可知，作者认为：批评和质疑这样的机制是合情合理的，但明智的做法是带着感激和感恩之心来接受这些奖项。由此可知，A选项为作者对the new awards态度的合理概括。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】B 对科研文化是有害的：选项利用5段4句中的the culture of research设置干扰，该句提出“批评和质疑这样的机制合情合理的——毕竟这是一种科研文化”，但并未提及新奖项对科研文化有害（harmful），因此该选项不符合文意，故排除。

【无中生有】C选项和D选项在原文中并未出现，属于无中生有，故排除。

sections.title: 阅读Text4
sections.passage:
1 " The Heart of the Matter," the just-released report by the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (AAAS), deserves praise for affirming the importance of the humanities and social sciences to the prosperity and security of liberal democracy in America. 2 Regrettably, however, the report ’s failure to address the true nature of the crisis facing liberal education may cause more harm than good.?
1 In 2010, leading congressional Democrats and Republicans sent letters to the AAAS asking that it identify actions that could be taken by "federal, state and local governments, universities, foundations, educators, individual benefactors and others" to " maintain national excellence in humanities and social scientific scholarship and education."? 2 In response, the American Academy formed the Commission on the Humanities and Social Sciences. 3 Among the commission’s 51 members are top-tier-university presidents, scholars, lawyers, judges, and business executives, as well as prominent figures from diplomacy, filmmaking, music and journalism.
1 The goals identified in the report are generally admirable. 2 Because representative government presupposes an informed citizenry, the report supports full literacy; stresses the study of history and government, particularly American history and American government; and encourages the use of new digital technologies.? 3 To encourage innovation and competition, the report calls for increased investment in research, the crafting of coherent curricula that improve students’ ability to solve problems and communicate effectively in the 21st century, increased funding for teachers and the encouragement of scholars to bring their learning to bear on the great challenges of the day. 4 The report also advocates greater study of foreign languages, international affairs and the expansion of study abroad programs.
1 Unfortunately, despite 2½ years in the making, " The Heart of the Matter " never gets to the heart of the matter: the illiberal nature of liberal education at our leading colleges and universities. 2 The commission ignores that for several decades America 's colleges and universities have produced graduates who don’t know the content and character of liberal education and are thus deprived of its benefits. 3 Sadly, the spirit of inquiry once at home on campus has been replaced by the use of the humanities and social sciences as vehicles for publicizing "progressive," or left-liberal propaganda.
1 Today, professors routinely treat the progressive interpretation of history and progressive public policy as the proper subject of study while portraying conservative or classical liberal ideas — such as free markets and self-reliance — as falling outside the boundaries of routine, and sometimes legitimate, intellectual investigation.?
1 The AAAS displays great enthusiasm for liberal education. 2 Yet its report may well set back reform by obscuring the depth and breadth of the challenge that Congress asked it to illuminate.?

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

According to Paragraph 1, what is the author’s attitude toward the AAAS’s report？

根据第一段，作者对美国人文与科学院报告的态度是什么?

A. Critical   批评的

B. Appreciative    赞赏的

C. Contemptuous    轻蔑的

D. Tolerant    宽容的


【定位及答案】

根据题干直接定位在1段。题目问的是作者对于AAAS’s report的态度，1段1句提到该报告deserves praise（值得称赞），但2句中出现了Regrettably（令人遗憾地）和however（然而），可见作者对该报告的评价并非完全持称赞态度，根据后面提到的“这份报告未能解决人文教育所面临的危机的本质”，以及cause more harm than good（弊大于利），可进一步确定作者对该报告的态度是批评多于赞赏的，因此A选项正确。


【错选分析】

【以偏概全】B 赞赏的：该选项最具迷惑性，因为1段1句中提到...，deserves praise...，很容易根据赞扬选择与之意思相近的B选项Appreciative（赞赏的），但此题考查作者的观点转变，应该综合全段做出合理推断，尤其要注意语义转折之处。由1段2句可知，B选项以偏概全，故排除。

【无中生有】C选项和D选项在原文没有依据，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Influential figures in the Congress required   that the AAAS report on how to______ .

国会重要人物要求美国人文与科学院就如何______ 给出报告。

A. retain people's interest in liberal education

   维持人们对人文教育的兴趣

B. define the government’s role in education

   明确政府在教育中的作用

C. keep a leading position in liberal education

   保持在人文教育的领先地位

D. safeguard individuals’ rights to education

   保障个人受教育的权利


【定位及答案】

根据题干中的Congress定位到2段1句。题干中的Influential figures in the Congress对应原文2段1句中的leading congressional Democrats and Republicans；题干中的required that对应2段1句的asking that（要求），而C选项keep a leading position in liberal education（保持在人文教育的领先地位）刚好是2段1句中maintain national excellence in humanities...and education（维护国家在人文科学和……教育方面的卓越成就）的同义转述，因此C选项为正确答案。


【错选分析】

【词汇干扰】B 明确政府在教育中的作用：选项利用2段1句中的governments一词设置干扰，但该句意为要求AAAS明确“联邦、州和地方政府……”可以采取的行动，而不是B选项所指的明确政府在教育中的作用，因此B选项错误。

【无中生有】A选项和D选项在原文中并无相关信息，属于无中生有，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

According to Paragraph 3，the report suggests______ .

根据第三段, 报告建议______ 。

A. an exclusive study of American history

   对美国历史进行专门研究

B. a greater emphasis on theoretical subjects

   更加强调理论学科

C. the application of emerging technologies

   运用新兴科技

D. funding for the study of foreign languages

   资助外语研究


【定位及答案】

根据题干直接定位到第3段，该段讲述了报告中值得称道的目标，即报告的相关建议。其中2句指出“该报告……鼓励使用最新的数字技术”，C选项与之表述相符，故为正确答案。其中，the application of为2句中the use of的同义替换，emerging technologies与文中的new digital technologies对应。


【错选分析】

【偷换概念】A 对美国历史进行专门研究：利用3段2句中的American history设置干扰，该句强调“学习历史知识以及政府相关的知识，特别是美国历史和美国政府”，并未指出要“对美国历史进行专门研究”，故排除。

【无中生有】B 更加强调理论学科：选项在原文中没有依据，故排除。

【张冠李戴】D 资助外语研究：利用3段3句中的funding for和4句中的study of foreign languages设置干扰，原文中funding for的对象是teachers，并非“外语研究”，故D选项错误。

【题目及选项概览】

The author implies in Paragraph 5 that professors are______ .

作者在第5段中暗示，教授们______。

A. supportive of free markets

   支持自由市场

B. cautious about intellectual investigation

   谨慎对待学术研究

C. conservative about public policy

   保守对待公共政策

D. biased against classical liberal ideas

   对传统的自由理念持有偏见


【定位及答案】

根题干定位到第5段，由题干中的implies可知此题属于推理判断题，应仔细比对各选项与该段内容。分析该段内容，while之前提及“教授们通常将进步的历史观和公共政策视为适当的研究课题”，而while之后却说“教授们通常把……保守或传统的自由理念描述为违背常规……”。通过前后这两种态度的对比，可看出教授反对传统的自由理念，认为其违背常规，即对传统的自由理念持有偏见。因此，D选项正确。


【错选分析】

【反向干扰】A 支持自由市场：由原文可知，教授们认为“自由市场是保守的，且违背常规”，故不可能对其持支持态度，故排除。

【无中生有】B 谨慎对待学术研究：选项利用五段出现的intellectual investigation设置干扰，但cautious about在原文没有依据，故排除。

【偷换概念】C 保守对待公共政策：原文明确指出“教授们将进步的公共政策视为适当的研究课题”，而非“保守对待公共政策”，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题目及选项概览】

Which of the following would be the best title for the text？

本文最合适的标题是什么？

A. Ways to Grasp“The Heart of the Matter”

   把握“问题核心”的方法

B. Illiberal Education and “The Heart of the Matter”

   非人文教育和“问题核心”

C. The AAAS's Contribution to Liberal Education

   美国艺术与科学院对人文教育的贡献

D. Progressive Policy vs. Liberal Education

   进步政策与人文教育


【定位及答案】

本题要求考生选择文章的最佳标题，属于判断主旨大意类题目，测试考生对文章大意的把握。解题时要注意文章中出现的高频关键词，这往往是表达主题的主要措辞。这篇短文出现频率最高的是the report，即“The Heart of the Matter”（“问题核心”报告）。文章主要阐述的是“问题核心”报告并未解决美国人文教育（Liberal Education）非人文这一本质问题，即美国的人文教育实际上是非人文的教育（Illiberal Education），故B选项是概括全文主题最恰当的标题。


【错选分析】

【答非所问】A 把握“问题核心”的方法：选项提到了“The Heart of the Matter”报告，但是文章并不是具体分析把握“问题核心”的方法，而是论述“问题核心”报告存在的问题，故排除。

【以偏概全】C选项和D选项分别源自文章第3段和第5段，但其均不能概栝全文的中心思想，故均不是文章合适的标题。

sections.title: 翻译
sections.passage:
1 Within the span of a hundred years, in the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, a tide of emigration — one of the great folk wanderings of history — swept from Europe to America. 2 This movement, driven by powerful and diverse motivations, built a nation out of a wilderness and, by its nature, shaped the character and destiny of an uncharted continent.?
1 The United States is the product of two principal forces — the immigration of European peoples with their varied ideas, customs, and national characteristics and the impact of a new country which modified these traits.? 2 Of necessity, colonial America was a projection of Europe. 3 Across the Atlantic came successive groups of Englishmen, Frenchmen, Germans, Scots, Irishmen, Dutchmen, Swedes, and many others who attempted to transplant their habits and traditions to the new world. 4 But the force of geographic conditions peculiar to America, the interplay of the varied national groups upon one another, and the sheer difficulty of maintaining old-world ways in a raw, new continent caused significant changes.? 5 These changes were gradual and at first scarcely visible. 6 But the result was a new social pattern which, although it resembled European society in many ways, had a character that was distinctly American.
1 The first shiploads of immigrants bound for the territory which is now the United States crossed the Atlantic more than a hundred years after the 15th-and-16th-century explorations of North America.? 2 In the meantime, thriving Spanish colonies had been established in Mexico, the West Indies, and South America. 3 These travelers to North America came in small, unmercifully overcrowded craft. 4 During their six-to-twelve-week voyage, they survived on barely enough food allotted to them. 5 Many of the ships were lost in storms, many passengers died of disease, and infants rarely survived the journey. 6 Sometimes storms blew the vessels far off their course, and often calm brought unbearably long delay.
1 To the anxious travelers the sight of the American shore brought almost inexpressible relief. 2 Said one recorder of events, “ The air at twelve leagues ’ distance smelt as sweet as a new-blown garden. ” 3 The colonists ’ first glimpse of the new land was a sight of dense woods. 4 The virgin forest with its richness and variety of trees was a real treasure-house which extended from Maine all the way down to Georgia.? 5 Here was abundant fuel and lumber. 6 Here was the raw material of houses and furniture, ships and potash, dyes and naval stores.

questions.stem:
① 在十七到十八世纪初期的一百年间，一股移民浪潮——一次史上重大的民间迁移——从欧洲横扫至美洲。②在各种强大动机的推动下，这场迁移从荒野中造就了一个民族，并循其本质塑造了一片全新大陆的特点，决定了它的命运。
① 美国是两股主要力量作用的产物：一是具有不同思想、风俗和民族特点的欧洲各民族的迁入，二是一个新国家因改变了这些特征而产生的影响。②不可避免地，殖民地时期的美洲是欧洲的投影。③ 成群的英格兰人、法国人、德国人、苏格兰人、爱尔兰人、荷兰人、瑞典人和许多其他民族的人络绎不绝地横穿过大西洋，企图把他们的习惯和传统照搬到新世界里。④ 但美洲特有地理条件的作用，不同族群间的相互影响，加上在一片蛮荒新大陆上维持旧大陆方式的巨大困难，所有这一切引起了意义深远的变化。⑤ 这些变化是渐进的，最初几乎不明显。⑥ 但结果是形成了一种新的社会模式，尽管它在很多方面与欧洲社会相似，但却具有明显的美国特色。
①在十五、十六世纪的北美大陆探险过去一百多年后，首批满载移民驶向今天合众国这片疆土的船只横穿过了大西洋。②与此同时，繁荣的西班牙殖民地在墨西哥、西印度群岛和南美洲已经建立起来。③这些奔赴北美洲的旅客乘坐狭小、极度拥挤的船而来。④ 在6到12周的航行中，他们靠分给的勉强能糊口的食物幸存下来。⑤ 许多船只迷失在风暴之中，大量乘客死于疾病，婴幼儿在旅途中几乎无一幸存。⑥有时候风暴刮得船远远偏离航线，而平静无风又常常带来难以忍受的长久性耽搁。
①对于这些焦虑的旅客来说，看见美国海岸的那一刻带来的如释重负之感几乎难以形容。② 某位事件记录者说道：“十二里格外的空气闻起来就像花朵新盛开的花园一样芬芳。”③这些殖民者第一眼瞥见的是这片新大陆上的茂密森林。④ 郁郁葱葱、树种繁多的原始森林是一座从缅因一直向南绵延到佐治亚的天然宝库。⑤ 这里有丰富的燃料和木材。⑥这里有建造房子、家具和船只以及生产钾碱、染料和松脂制品的原材料。
questions.answer: 在多种强大动机的驱使下,这场运动在荒野上建立起一个国家,并且从本质上而言,塑造了一片未知大陆的性格和命运.
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“This movement, driven by powerful and diverse motivations,”此处This movement为整个句子的主语，driven...by是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰主语翻译为在...驱使下， 此外，powerful and diversi（多种强大的）是and连接的两个并列形容词，作前置定语修饰motivatio，翻译时按顺序译出即可。“built a nation out of a wilderness ”此处是and连接的第一个谓宾部分，其中out of a wildernes是介词短语作地点状语，out of是from的意思，wilderness译为荒野、荒漠、沙地。“and, by its nature, shaped the character and destiny of an uncharted continent.”此处是and连接的第二个谓宾部分，介词短语by its nature作插入语，译为从本质上而言，“of an uncharted continent”为介词短语作后置定语修饰 the character and destiny ，其中uncharted continent可译为地图上未标明的大陆、未知大陆。

questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“The United States is the product of two principal forces”为本句主干，是个主系表结构，其中of two principal forces作后置定语，修饰前面的the product此部分翻译时可直接采用主系表结构“美国是...的产物”。“of European peoples”为介词短语作后置定语修饰the immigrant，即译为欧洲民族移民，“with their varied ideas, customs, and national characteristics ”为介词短语作后置定语修饰European peoples ，其中介词with可以直接处理为动词“带来...;带来...""of a new country "为介词短语作后置定语修饰impact可译为...的影响。同时后面又嵌套一个which引导的定语从句修饰a new country即译为修改这些特性的新兴国家。

questions.answer: 然而，美国特有的地理条件、不同民族间的相互作用以及在这片原始的新大陆上维持旧秩序的高难度，这些（因素）导致了巨大的变化。
questions.explanation:
【句子结构分析】

“But the force of geographic conditions peculiar to America,” 这部分中“ of geographic conditions peculiar to America”为介词短语作后置定语修饰the force，其中形容词短语peculiar to American又作geographic conditions 的后置定语，处理起来为美国特有的地理条件的力量，但...条件的力量不太符合汉语的表达习惯，所以可将force省略不译。“of the varied national groups ”为介词短语作后置定语修饰the interplay，介词短语upon one another 同样作the interplay的后置定语，译为彼此之间。“the sheer difficulty of maintaining old-world ways in a raw, new continent”中，sheer修饰difficulty用于加强语气，译为非常，极其，in a raw，new continent为地点状语修饰maintaining，翻译时可以放在被修饰成分前面，译为在一个原始的新大陆上维持...”。
